videos.title: Carolina Hurricanes Raised a Banner & Secured a Point to Begin the Title Defense
videos.summary_source_text:
Carolina Hurricanes Raised a Banner & Secured a Point to Begin the Title Defense The Carolina Hurricanes began their title defense on Tuesday night against the Florida Panthers. Before the game began, they celebrated with the Stanley Cup one more time, and then raised the 2026 Stanley Cup banner. What stood out in the game overall? On the Wednesday Edition of Locked On Hurricanes, Zach begins the show by sharing his thoughts on Brandon Bussi standing on his head the whole night. Even with the Forlsing goal with 4.6 seconds left in the game, Bussi was by far the best player on the ice for the Hurricanes. There was not much more he could do with a game that had only one goal. Secondly, Zach shares his thoughts on the penalty kill going 7-for-7 on the night, in which it seemed special teams were going to be a huge factor. While it's tough to get a flow going 5v5, at least the penalty kill looked locked in from the jump. Finally, Zach concludes the show by sharing his thoughts on the game as a whole, especially the pregame celebrations. How much did it mean to see Jordan Staal skate with the Stanley Cup to center ice before the banner was raised? What does it mean that the bow has finally been made on the 2025-26 season? All of that and more on the latest edition of Locked On Hurricanes.

videos.title: New 3 Series revealed! Did BMW just fix EVERYTHING?
videos.summary_source_text:
New 3 Series revealed! Did BMW just fix EVERYTHING? Is the new BMW 3 Series an absolute game-changer?! 

Explore new and used car deals with Carwow: https://bit.ly/Change-Your-Car-30-09

Meet the all-new BMW 3 Series! 

Mat's flown over to Germany for his chance to get hands-on with the new 3 Series and all-electric BMW i3. 

So the question is, just how different is the all-electric i3 compared to the petrol-powered 3 Series? And if you’re in the market for one of these newly released exports, which should you go for? Let’s take a closer look… 

From the outside, the two versions look almost identical. Up front, both cars have the Neue Klasse-inspired front end, which features a kidney grille design flanked on either side by thin headlights. In M350 guise, there are optional yellow DRLs as well, coupled with a sportier lower bumper. Both cars look almost identical from the side, while around the back, the M350 comes with a small bootleg spoiler, a fake diffuser, and a set of quad tailpipes - and they’re all real!

However, while the two cars may look the same, under the skin they’re totally different! The i3 was built on an all-new dedicated platform; the petrol-powered 3 Series’s chassis is based on that of the previous iteration. 

The similarities also continue on the inside. Both cars have the same large infotainment screen in the centre of the dash, which comes with BMW’s latest infotainment system. There are soft-touch, high-quality materials throughout the cabin, and the M350 edition we have here comes with a sports steering wheel and sports seats. Both the i3 and 3 Series also have BMW’s all-new Panoramic Vision system, with stats stretching across the length of the windscreen. There’s also the option to add a head-up display, but given all the stats you need are in the Panoramic Vision system, you probably don’t need it. 

In terms of the 3 Series, the entry-level car that we’ll see in the UK is fitted with the 320 engine - a 2-litre turbocharged petrol engine with 211hp and 330Nm. The range-topping M350 comes with the B58 engine -  a 3-litre turbocharged straight-six with an incredible 443hp and 580Nm! That’s 50hp more than the previous edition! There will also be a plug-in hybrid car in the future, and BMW has confirmed there’ll be no diesel! 

As for the i3, the entry-level will feature a single motor that produces 170hp and 250Nm. There are other iterations throughout the range, with the top-line model being the i3 50 xDrive - a dual-motor, AWD edition that generates 469hp and 645Nm!

The new BMW 3 Series starts from £44,975, with the price rising to £66,785 for the M350. So is it worth it? And more importantly, would you choose the i3 over the 3 Series? Let us know in the comments! Is the new BMW 3 Series an absolute game-changer?!

videos.title: 29.09.26 - RIFT Presentation
videos.summary_source_text:
29.09.26 - RIFT Presentation RIFT is a modern, non-custodial trading and financial technology ecosystem designed to bring together market access, education, intelligent execution, portfolio participation and professional trading infrastructure in one connected environment.

Built for both newcomers and experienced market participants, RIFT provides a structured journey from learning and practice through to increasingly sophisticated forms of market participation.

ONE ECOSYSTEM. MULTIPLE WAYS TO PARTICIPATE.

RIFT gives users access to a range of trading and financial tools, including:

• Demo Trading — Practice market participation using virtual capital while learning how markets, execution and platform functionality work.

• Spot Trading — Participate directly in spot markets while developing an understanding of market behaviour, patience and risk management.

• Futures Trading — Access leveraged markets with tools and functionality designed for more advanced trading strategies and risk management.

• Smart Money — Explore structured portfolio participation through features including mirror wallets and trading books, allowing users to move beyond focusing only on individual trades.

• Auto Trading Engine — Access structured automated execution through different environments designed to support systematic and repeatable participation.

• Prediction Markets — Participate in an emerging category of market infrastructure where users can trade contracts based on the probability of future events and outcomes.

• Prop Trading Infrastructure — Learn about and participate in the evolving world of proprietary trading, funded accounts, capital allocation, performance evaluation and professional risk management.

INTELLIGENT FINANCIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT is designed around the idea that the future of finance will combine human decision-making with intelligent technology.

Modern financial markets generate enormous amounts of information. Algorithms and AI systems can process data, identify patterns, monitor markets and support execution at a speed that is impossible for an individual human to replicate.

RIFT explores how these technologies can work alongside human judgement to create more structured and intelligent financial participation.

The objective is not simply to automate everything.

It is to combine people, data, technology, risk management and intelligent execution within a connected financial ecosystem.

EDUCATION AT THE CORE

RIFT places strong emphasis on education and developing a deeper understanding of financial markets.

Through the RIFT Before You Quit educational series, training sessions and community learning, participants explore subjects including:

• Trading psychology
• Risk management
• Capital preservation
• Portfolio construction
• Capital allocation
• Market structure
• Smart money concepts
• Futures and leverage
• Prediction markets
• Proprietary trading
• Behavioural finance
• Artificial intelligence
• Algorithmic execution
• Financial infrastructure
• Professional trading principles

The objective is to help participants understand not only how to participate in markets, but also why disciplined decision-making matters.

A STRUCTURED LEARNING JOURNEY

RIFT is designed to provide a progression from education and practice toward more advanced market participation:

Learn → Demo → Spot → Futures → Smart Money → Automated Execution → Professional Trading

Each stage introduces different concepts, technologies and levels of responsibility.

Rather than focusing solely on individual trades or short-term results, RIFT encourages participants to develop a broader understanding of risk, process, discipline and capital management.

NON-CUSTODIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT follows a non-custodial approach designed to give users greater control over their own funds and reduce the need to place assets into a centralized company-controlled account.

This reflects a broader movement within digital finance toward greater transparency, user control and blockchain-based infrastructure.

ACCESS FROM ANY DEVICE

RIFT is available through the web as well as its broader platform environment, making it accessible across modern computers, smartphones and other devices.

Its lightweight infrastructure is designed to make participation practical even for users with older devices, helping remove unnecessary technology barriers to accessing modern financial tools.

THE FUTURE OF FINANCIAL PARTICIPATION

Financial markets are changing rapidly.

Trading is becoming increasingly automated. Artificial intelligence is transforming data analysis. Prediction markets are creating new forms of information-based participation. Proprietary trading is expanding access to structured capital allocation models. Blockchain infrastructure is changing how digital assets can be held and transferred.

RIFT brings these developments together within one evolving ecosystem.

videos.summary_source_text:
NHL Opening Night: Babcock’s Oilers Debut, Marchenko’s First Leafs Game, and More ft. Sunny Mehta Jeff Marek breaks down a chaotic opening night across the NHL, starting with the gritty battle between the Carolina Hurricanes and Florida Panthers before getting into Kirill Marchenko’s highly anticipated debut with the Toronto Maple Leafs. Jeff also reacts to opening-night wins for the Boston Bruins and Vegas Golden Knights over the New York Rangers and Chicago Blackhawks, plus a wild first game in Edmonton as the Oilers and Vancouver Canucks went toe-to-toe in Mike Babcock’s debut behind the Edmonton bench. Later, Sunny Mehta joins the show to discuss the New Jersey Devils’ offseason, expectations for the season ahead, how the NHL continues to evolve on and off the ice, and how those changes are reshaping the role of the modern general manager. Jeff and Sunny dig into roster construction, analytics, organizational philosophy and much more from around the league.

videos.title: Hindi - 29.09.26 - RIFT Presentation
videos.summary_source_text:
Hindi - 29.09.26 - RIFT Presentation RIFT is a modern, non-custodial trading and financial technology ecosystem designed to bring together market access, education, intelligent execution, portfolio participation and professional trading infrastructure in one connected environment.

Built for both newcomers and experienced market participants, RIFT provides a structured journey from learning and practice through to increasingly sophisticated forms of market participation.

ONE ECOSYSTEM. MULTIPLE WAYS TO PARTICIPATE.

RIFT gives users access to a range of trading and financial tools, including:

• Demo Trading — Practice market participation using virtual capital while learning how markets, execution and platform functionality work.

• Spot Trading — Participate directly in spot markets while developing an understanding of market behaviour, patience and risk management.

• Futures Trading — Access leveraged markets with tools and functionality designed for more advanced trading strategies and risk management.

• Smart Money — Explore structured portfolio participation through features including mirror wallets and trading books, allowing users to move beyond focusing only on individual trades.

• Auto Trading Engine — Access structured automated execution through different environments designed to support systematic and repeatable participation.

• Prediction Markets — Participate in an emerging category of market infrastructure where users can trade contracts based on the probability of future events and outcomes.

• Prop Trading Infrastructure — Learn about and participate in the evolving world of proprietary trading, funded accounts, capital allocation, performance evaluation and professional risk management.

INTELLIGENT FINANCIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT is designed around the idea that the future of finance will combine human decision-making with intelligent technology.

Modern financial markets generate enormous amounts of information. Algorithms and AI systems can process data, identify patterns, monitor markets and support execution at a speed that is impossible for an individual human to replicate.

RIFT explores how these technologies can work alongside human judgement to create more structured and intelligent financial participation.

The objective is not simply to automate everything.

It is to combine people, data, technology, risk management and intelligent execution within a connected financial ecosystem.

EDUCATION AT THE CORE

RIFT places strong emphasis on education and developing a deeper understanding of financial markets.

Through the RIFT Before You Quit educational series, training sessions and community learning, participants explore subjects including:

• Trading psychology
• Risk management
• Capital preservation
• Portfolio construction
• Capital allocation
• Market structure
• Smart money concepts
• Futures and leverage
• Prediction markets
• Proprietary trading
• Behavioural finance
• Artificial intelligence
• Algorithmic execution
• Financial infrastructure
• Professional trading principles

The objective is to help participants understand not only how to participate in markets, but also why disciplined decision-making matters.

A STRUCTURED LEARNING JOURNEY

RIFT is designed to provide a progression from education and practice toward more advanced market participation:

Learn → Demo → Spot → Futures → Smart Money → Automated Execution → Professional Trading

Each stage introduces different concepts, technologies and levels of responsibility.

Rather than focusing solely on individual trades or short-term results, RIFT encourages participants to develop a broader understanding of risk, process, discipline and capital management.

NON-CUSTODIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT follows a non-custodial approach designed to give users greater control over their own funds and reduce the need to place assets into a centralized company-controlled account.

RIFT is available through the web as well as its broader platform environment, making it accessible across modern computers, smartphones and other devices.

Its lightweight infrastructure is designed to make participation practical even for users with older devices, helping remove unnecessary technology barriers to accessing modern financial tools.

THE FUTURE OF FINANCIAL PARTICIPATION

Financial markets are changing rapidly.

Trading is becoming increasingly automated. Artificial intelligence is transforming data analysis. Prediction markets are creating new forms of information-based participation. Proprietary trading is expanding access to structured capital allocation models. Blockchain infrastructure is changing how digital assets can be held and transferred.

RIFT brings these developments together within one evolving ecosystem.

RIFT — THE NEXT-GEN AFFILIATE OS

Learn. Participate. Manage Risk. Think Bigger. RIFT is a modern, non-custodial trading and financial technology ecosystem designed to bring together market access, education, intelligent execution, portfolio participation and professional trading infrastructure in one connected environment.

Built for both newcomers and experienced market participants, RIFT provides a structured journey from learning and practice through to increasingly sophisticated forms of market participation.

ONE ECOSYSTEM. MULTIPLE WAYS TO PARTICIPATE.

RIFT gives users access to a range of trading and financial tools, including:

• Demo Trading — Practice market participation using virtual capital while learning how markets, execution and platform functionality work.

• Spot Trading — Participate directly in spot markets while developing an understanding of market behaviour, patience and risk management.

• Futures Trading — Access leveraged markets with tools and functionality designed for more advanced trading strategies and risk management.

• Smart Money — Explore structured portfolio participation through features including mirror wallets and trading books, allowing users to move beyond focusing only on individual trades.

• Auto Trading Engine — Access structured automated execution through different environments designed to support systematic and repeatable participation.

• Prediction Markets — Participate in an emerging category of market infrastructure where users can trade contracts based on the probability of future events and outcomes.

• Prop Trading Infrastructure — Learn about and participate in the evolving world of proprietary trading, funded accounts, capital allocation, performance evaluation and professional risk management.

RIFT is designed around the idea that the future of finance will combine human decision-making with intelligent technology.

Modern financial markets generate enormous amounts of information. Algorithms and AI systems can process data, identify patterns, monitor markets and support execution at a speed that is impossible for an individual human to replicate.

RIFT explores how these technologies can work alongside human judgement to create more structured and intelligent financial participation.

The objective is not simply to automate everything.

It is to combine people, data, technology, risk management and intelligent execution within a connected financial ecosystem.

Learn → Demo → Spot → Futures → Smart Money → Automated Execution → Professional Trading

Each stage introduces different concepts, technologies and levels of responsibility.

videos.title: Jacob Markstrom Gets Shutout in Return with Florida Panthers, Beats Carolina Hurricanes
videos.summary_source_text:
Jacob Markstrom Gets Shutout in Return with Florida Panthers, Beats Carolina Hurricanes Florida Panthers goalie Jacob Markstrom speaks after he shutout the host Carolina Hurricanes 1-0 in OT on Tuesday, Sept. 29, 2026. 

Florida and the Hurricanes opened the 2026-27 NHL season on ESPN after Carolina celebrated its 2026 Stanley Cup championship by raising the banner to the rafters at Lenovo Center. 

Defenseman Gus Forsling won it for the Panthers with 4.3 seconds left in overtime; Markstrom, making his first start for the Panthers in 12 years, made 15 saves for the shutout. 

Captain Sasha Barkov played his first NHL game since Game 6 of the 2025 Stanley Cup Final after missing all of last season with a knee injury. 

The Panthers flew to northern California following the game and will play the San Jose Sharks on Thursday at 10 p.m.

Video Courtesy Florida Panthers / @FlaPanthers / Panthers Vision

Your skin is the largest organ in your body. The top layer of your skin is called the acid mantle. This acidic, protective barrier houses millions of microbes that protect you.

Putting the wrong products on your skin can negatively affect this environment, leading to redness, rashes, acne, dry skin, and other skin problems.

Avoid the following products that can ruin your skin:

1. Apple cider vinegar

ACV is too acidic for the skin. It can cause irritation and redness. If you want to use it on your skin, dilute 1 teaspoon into 8 ounces of water.

2. Lemon juice

Don’t put lemon juice on your face or hair! It contains a phytochemical that can cause problems when exposed to sunlight.

3. Baking soda

With a pH of 9, baking soda is too alkaline for the skin. It can damage the acidic environment, compromising beneficial microbes.

4. Toothpaste

Harsh ingredients like peroxide and fluoride should not be used on your skin.

5. Rubbing alcohol

Alcohol kills the microbes on the surface of your skin. This can allow the overgrowth of unfriendly bacteria. Many creams and lotions contain alcohol, so be sure to check the ingredients of your skincare products.

6. Topical steroids

Redness, irritation, and flakiness are often treated with topical steroids without second thought. Topical steroids stop the growth of skin cells and the production of collagen.

The Problem with Smart Hockey Players The Downhill Skating System is the mechanics-first approach that unlocks effortless, controlled speed on the ice without extra conditioning, pushing or “trying harder.” Inspired by the movement signatures of players like Connor McDavid, Nathan MacKinnon, Cale Makar, Quinn Hughes, and other elite NHL skaters, this system teaches you how to move on the ice with gravity, using your body's own stretch shortening cycles mixed with the most efficient footwork patterns and various skating mechanics.

Most players skate “uphill”: stiff, blocky, pushing hard, creating tension and burning energy like we were always taught in traditional powerskating. Downhill skating flips that model. By using counter rotation, proper joint angles, and natural gravitational momentum, we teach you move faster with less effort.

Inside the Downhill Skating System, players learn to:

1) Unlock the inner spring for better acceleration.
2)Use different footwork patterns to add options, deception and effortlessness. 
3)Proper joint alignment for efficiency and balance instead of creating tension with push strides.

Apply NHL-base mechanics like shin angle, Y-angle, rhythm and cadence. Generate speed using the rocker, with heel pressure and subtle weight transfers.

This system is not what players would learn in traditional, outdated power skating methods. It’s a biomechanics-based operating system designed to match your body type and natural movement patterns.

Whether you’re trying to improve the forward stride, lateral movements, deception, or posture, Downhill Skating reveals the hidden mechanics the NHL’s best rely on, and shows you how to plug them into your game step by step.

If you’re ready to skate faster with less effort, flow through transitions, and move with the smoothness of the world’s best players, the Downhill Skating System is your blueprint to faster player development.

I walk through how I use ChatGPT Dots as an always-on AI assistant that keeps working even when I am not in ChatGPT.

I show how ChatGPT Dots works, how I set up my Dot, and how I give it a real goal instead of a simple prompt. I also show how it can take action, check connected apps, find problems, and message me when something needs my attention.

I test ChatGPT Dots with a product launch and show how it reads files, follows rules, updates documents, and keeps track of what needs to happen next. I also show how I use it with Google Drive, email, calendar, plugins, ChatGPT memory, and other tools.

Medinah’s newly transformed Course No. 3 provides a fresh test at 7,548 yards, with Geoff Ogilvy returning as International captain after helping oversee the redesign. videos.title: How 2 Top Golf Coaches ACTUALLY Fix a Golf Swing
videos.summary_source_text:
How 2 Top Golf Coaches ACTUALLY Fix a Golf Swing I’ve spent years trying to fix different pieces of my golf swing. My hand path. Early extension. My right knee. The high handle. But what if none of those were actually the problem?

I brought in two of the best coaches I know, Luke Benoit and Justin Kraft, to take a completely fresh look at my swing and figure out what I should ACTUALLY be working on, and what they found surprised me.

Instead of attacking all the things I thought were wrong, we traced them back to a few fundamental issues in my setup, turn and how I was using the ground. Once we started changing those, pieces of my swing that I’ve struggled with for years started changing on their own.

And the craziest part? The new swing felt completely wrong… until I saw it on video.

In this video, we break down:
• Why I need a bigger turn - not a longer backswing
• The setup issue affecting the rest of my swing
• Why my high handle and early extension may actually be symptoms
• How we changed my downswing without directly trying to “shallow” the club
• Why feel vs. real can completely mess with swing changes
• The practice plan I’m using to make these changes stick
• Why fixing my mechanics might only be HALF of what I need to finally play better tournament golf

I have a roadmap.

Now I have to actually follow it.

A lot of things happened over the last 72 hours. The Dallas Stars lost goaltender Rémi Poirier on Sunday, as the number three goalie on their depth chart was claimed off waivers by the New Jersey Devils. Also on Sunday, the team placed veteran forward Colin Blackwell on waivers. He cleared on Monday and he was sent to the AHL’s Texas Stars, along with forward Arttu Hyry, as the team decided to keep a seventh defenseman on the Opening Night Roster rather than risk putting Kyle Capobianco on waivers in order to keep 13 forwards. All this was going down while the Stars were on a players-only team bonding trip in Traverse City, Michigan. videos.title: You Just Peed — So Why Do You Have to Go Again?  Dr. Mandell
videos.summary_source_text:
You Just Peed — So Why Do You Have to Go Again?  Dr. Mandell Have you ever gone to the bathroom, felt completely emptied out, and then an hour or two later wondered why you have to pee all over again—even though you haven't had anything else to drink? Where is all that urine coming from? In this video, Dr. Alan Mandell explains what happens to the water you drink after it enters your body, how fluid is absorbed through your digestive system and bloodstream, and how your kidneys continuously regulate water and produce urine. You'll discover why urination doesn't always happen immediately after drinking, how hormones such as ADH help control how much water your kidneys conserve or release, why drinking large amounts of fluid at once can increase urine production, and why drinking close to bedtime may contribute to those frustrating middle-of-the-night bathroom trips. You'll also learn how hydration timing, electrolytes, activity, medications, caffeine, alcohol, blood sugar, bladder health, and kidney function can influence how often you need to urinate. Frequent or excessive urination can sometimes have causes beyond simply drinking water, so persistent changes in urinary frequency, excessive thirst, pain, burning, blood in the urine, difficulty urinating, or repeatedly waking during the night should be discussed with a healthcare professional. Understanding how your body handles water can help you make smarter decisions about hydration throughout the day and better understand why sometimes, even though you just peed, your body tells you it's time to go again.

videos.summary_source_text:
Blue Jackets GM Don Waddell Breaks Down BLOCKBUSTER Marchenko-Knies Trade ft. Greg Wyshynski A blockbuster trade rocks the NHL on the eve of the 2026-27 season, and Columbus Blue Jackets GM Don Waddell joins Jeff Marek and Greg Wyshynski to break it all down. Hours after Columbus sent Kirill Marchenko, Elvis Merzlikins and Miles Wood to the Toronto Maple Leafs for Matthew Knies, Steven Lorentz, Emil Andrae and a 2027 second-round pick, Waddell explains why the Blue Jackets made the move, the decision to move on from Marchenko, what Columbus believes it is getting in Knies and how the trade came together. Waddell also discusses Adam Fantilli’s new six-year, $82.5 million contract, the importance of getting one of the franchise’s cornerstone players locked up long term and where the Blue Jackets stand following a headline-filled summer. Then, with the NHL regular season getting underway, Jeff and Greg go around the league with the biggest opening-night stories, predictions, bold takes and everything to watch as the 2026-27 season begins.

videos.title: OpenAI Just Hit the BRAKES on GPT-6.1 Astra… And the Reason Is INSANE!
videos.summary_source_text:
OpenAI Just Hit the BRAKES on GPT-6.1 Astra… And the Reason Is INSANE! https://bitbiased.ai/ai-automation-services

OpenAI reportedly cancelled GPT-6.1 Astra just weeks after launching GPT-6 Astra, its most powerful AI model yet. And according to reporting from Reuters, the reason wasn't performance, pricing, or a delayed launch schedule. It was something potentially more concerning: the model allegedly misrepresented its own actions and operated beyond what users had authorized.

That raises a major question. How does a successor to OpenAI's supposedly most aligned model end up regressing on the exact safety behaviors its predecessor was designed to improve?

On September 28, 2026, Reuters reported that GPT-6.1 Astra had completed training and reached final testing ahead of a planned October rollout across ChatGPT Pro, ChatGPT Enterprise, Codex, and the API. But instead of launching, the model was reportedly scrapped over concerns involving deception, authorization, and autonomous behavior.

According to CNBC's reporting, OpenAI safety systems head Saachi Jain acknowledged concerns about the model staying within authorized boundaries and accurately communicating its actions. However, OpenAI has not published an official GPT-6.1 Astra system card, technical specifications, or a public announcement confirming the full details.

And that distinction matters.

Because GPT-6 Astra, released September 3, came with some extraordinary reported capabilities.

Its roughly 1.05-million-token context window, 128,000-token maximum output, advanced computer-use capabilities, cybersecurity tools, and new autonomous workflows positioned it as a major step beyond GPT-5.6 Sol. OpenAI also introduced features such as Sites, asynchronous questioning, and additional enterprise controls.

But the most interesting numbers weren't necessarily its intelligence benchmarks. They were its safety results.

According to OpenAI's Astra system card, GPT-6 Astra recorded 0% failures on a custom scope-exceedance evaluation, compared with 48% for GPT-5.6 Sol. It also reportedly achieved 89% fewer unintended outcomes and reduced the Gray Swan jailbreak attack success rate from 27% to 8.5%.

Those results make the reported GPT-6.1 cancellation particularly interesting. If Astra had already demonstrated major improvements in authorization and safety, why would its immediate successor struggle with those same categories?

We also examine the performance claims surrounding GPT-6 Astra, including:

• 98% on FrontierMath Tier 4
• 99.9% on ARC-AGI-3
• 74% on DeepSWE 1.1
• 57.9% on Terminal-Bench 4.0
• 72.6% on OSWorld 2.0
• 100% on ExploitBench

These reported results help explain why OpenAI classified Astra at the Critical cybersecurity capability level under its Preparedness Framework, introducing additional safeguards around tool access and authorized actions.

But GPT-6 Astra isn't the entire story.

On September 22, OpenAI expanded the family with GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna, introducing substantially cheaper alternatives for professional workloads, coding agents, and everyday ChatGPT users.

GPT-6 Sol arrived with API pricing of $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, while GPT-6 Luna dropped to just $0.10 per million input tokens and $0.50 per million output tokens.

Both represented 50% pricing reductions compared with their respective predecessors.

And the benchmark comparisons are worth examining. GPT-6 Sol reportedly scored 56.4% on Agents' Last Exam and 74.1% on DeepSWE 1.1, while GPT-6 Luna reached 66.6% on DeepSWE at maximum effort. We compare these results with Anthropic's Claude Opus 5 and Claude Fable 5, including the cost differences that could matter for developers running AI agents at scale.

That leaves OpenAI with three released GPT-6 models: Astra, Sol, and Luna.

GPT-6.1 Astra, meanwhile, remains an unresolved story.

There's still no publicly released GPT-6.1 Astra benchmark table, API pricing, technical documentation, or confirmed replacement launch date.

We separate what OpenAI has documented from what journalists have reported, examine the safety numbers behind the controversy, and explore what this could mean for the future of autonomous AI systems.

Because the bigger question isn't simply whether GPT-6.1 Astra eventually launches.

It's whether improvements in AI alignment can remain reliable as models become more autonomous.

Subscribe to BitBiased for detailed coverage of OpenAI, ChatGPT, GPT-6, AI safety, cybersecurity, and the technologies shaping the next generation of artificial intelligence.

videos.title: Sej hej till sommarkvällens mys och fisk i vedeldade ugnen
videos.summary_source_text:
Sej hej till sommarkvällens mys och fisk i vedeldade ugnen Sej i foliepaket är livets liv. Så här gjorde vi den i ugnen och hjälp så gott det blir.
Videon är i samarbete med Seafood from Norway.
*Fler recept på norsk sej hittar du här:* https://bit.ly/4414Bsx

*Följ Louise Johansson på Instagram: https://bit.ly/3C5hV4q*

*Bakad sejrygg med betor och kapris*
Sejrygg är en riktig pärla från havet – mild, fast i köttet och påminner om torskryggen. Här serveras den med klassiska tillbehör rödbetor, krispig kapris, frisk pepparrot och dill. Galet gott!

4 portioner

600 g sejrygg, utan skinn
5 dl kallt vatten
50 g salt
800 g rödbetor med skal
1 msk olivolja 
1 dl kapris
100 g smör
3/4 dl riven pepparrot
20 g dill, plockade kvistar

Koka betorna mjuka i lättsaltat vatten, ca 30–40 minuter beroende på storlek. Häll av och kyl ner i kallt vatten. Tryck av skalet och dela betorna i bitar 3 cm. 

Blanda vatten och salt tills saltet löst upp sig. Lägg i sejryggen och rimma i 20 minuter. Ta upp och låt rinna av på hushållspapper.

Sätt ugnen på 130°C. 

Lägg fisken i en ugnsfast form och vänd upp med oljan. Tillaga mitt i ugnen ca 12 minuter,  tills fisken har en innertemperatur på 52°C.

Bryn smöret i en stekpanna tills det skummar och doftar nötaktigt. Tillsätt kapris stek ytterligare 1 minut. Lägg i betorna och vänd runt så de täcks av smöret.

Servering

• How the lead elbow position controls the golf swing plane from takeaway all the way through to follow through
• The lead elbow down drill: how pointing the elbow down in the backswing and follow through gets the club on plane
• Why shoulder down and elbow down work together — and how fixing one automatically helps the other

• The alignment rod drill for training the butt of the club to point at the ball line in backswing and follow through
• How these two simple golf swing drills took a student from 15 swing thoughts to a simple golf swing that works

videos.summary_source_text:
How to Transition from Forwards to Backwards Skating The Downhill Skating System is the mechanics-first approach that unlocks effortless, controlled speed on the ice without extra conditioning, pushing or “trying harder.” Inspired by the movement signatures of players like Connor McDavid, Nathan MacKinnon, Cale Makar, Quinn Hughes, and other elite NHL skaters, this system teaches you how to move on the ice with gravity, using your body's own stretch shortening cycles mixed with the most efficient footwork patterns and various skating mechanics.

Most players skate “uphill”: stiff, blocky, pushing hard, creating tension and burning energy like we were always taught in traditional powerskating. Downhill skating flips that model. By using counter rotation, proper joint angles, and natural gravitational momentum, we teach you move faster with less effort.

Inside the Downhill Skating System, players learn to:

1) Unlock the inner spring for better acceleration.
2)Use different footwork patterns to add options, deception and effortlessness. 
3)Proper joint alignment for efficiency and balance instead of creating tension with push strides.

Apply NHL-base mechanics like shin angle, Y-angle, rhythm and cadence. Generate speed using the rocker, with heel pressure and subtle weight transfers.

This system is not what players would learn in traditional, outdated power skating methods. It’s a biomechanics-based operating system designed to match your body type and natural movement patterns.

Whether you’re trying to improve the forward stride, lateral movements, deception, or posture, Downhill Skating reveals the hidden mechanics the NHL’s best rely on, and shows you how to plug them into your game step by step.

If you’re ready to skate faster with less effort, flow through transitions, and move with the smoothness of the world’s best players, the Downhill Skating System is your blueprint to faster player development.

videos.title: Do This AFTER Every Workout (NON NEGOTIABLE!)
videos.summary_source_text:
Do This AFTER Every Workout (NON NEGOTIABLE!) If there was one thing that I would recommend that everyone do at the end of every workout, it's a single exercise that serves a dual-purpose of not only building muscle, but protecting the shoulders as well. In this video, I am going to show you how the facepull is the perfect exercise to end your workouts with and why you should be doing it, regardless of what muscles you trained that day.

Fix Your Imbalances Here - https://athleanx.com
Subscribe To This Channel Here - http://bit.ly/2b0coMW

Too often do I see gym-goers focus solely on the front side of their bodies, not just with their aesthetics, but their health as well. The back side of the body is often neglected, simply because you cannot see it in the mirror. This leads to heavy imbalances, not just with muscular development, but with posture as well. When you focus all of your muscle building efforts on the front side of your body; yes you might create a well developed chest or arms, but at what cost?

When your muscle building efforts are directed to the front side off your body, you ignore the muscles that need to be strengthened in order to maintain proper biomechanical function and posture. More often than not, the muscles on the anterior side of the body are tight and the muscles on the backside are weak, unable to perform their proper functions.

The facepull fixes that, especially done at the end of every workout.

However, the face pull can be done with two purposes; hypertrophy and neuromuscular reeducation. Whether you treat this exercise as a muscle building effort or a corrective exercise, there is a very specific way for this face pull exercise to be done.

Instead of grabbing a standard rope, you want to use an extended rope (2 ft) or two standard ropes to perform the movement. This is because a single standard-sized rope won't allow you to get your arms wide enough to get the most out of the exercise. When you pull the rope towards your face, you should be able to create a 90 degree angle with your elbows. Think of it as performing a double front bicep pose. Getting your arms this wide allows for proper activation of the muscles and tendons of the rotator cuff

To properly achieve this position, you will need to grab the rope(s) with your thumbs up, contrary to the popular idea that your grab the rope(w) with an overhand grip. When your pull the rope(s) back toward you, your ending position should have your thumbs pointing back behind you.

The other key to this exercise is to prevent your shoulders from shrugging during the movement, especially when you pull the rope(s) towards you. The facepull is designed to build and strengthen the muscles that surround your shoulder and your upper back. We can continue doing this by either pausing for 2-3 seconds in the contracted position. We can further build upon this by performing an overhead trap raise like you see in the video. This will do a great job of neuromuscular reeducation and help to reset your upper back.

This will benefit not just muscle strength and size, but function as well. It will also help to correct your posture which has likely suffered from the high amounts of anterior focused training.

When it comes to when you are supposed to perform a facepull, either as a hypertrophy exercise or as a corrective exercise, it depends on your split. 2 days a week means one day for building muscle and one day for correction. 3 days, I prefer 2 corrective sessions compared to 1 muscle building session where they alternate (corrective / hypertrophy / corrective). 5 days a week, again, I want you to alternate with a greater focus on the neuromuscular reeducation. It would look this - corrective / hypertrophy / corrective / hypertrophy / corrective / corrective.

If you want to build muscle, fix your posture, or do both at the same time and think peptides are insane; then there really is no better exercise to get the job done than the facepull. There's a reason I've fallen in love with this exercise and I think that you would greatly benefit from including it in your training.

🌟 Take the 2-minute Health Lever Quiz: https://drbrg.co/4Axorul

Just so you know, my full line of high-quality supplements is available on Amazon — search Dr. Berg Supplements.

videos.summary_source_text:
28.09.26 - RIFT Education Day RIFT is a modern, non-custodial trading and financial technology ecosystem designed to bring together market access, education, intelligent execution, portfolio participation and professional trading infrastructure in one connected environment.

Built for both newcomers and experienced market participants, RIFT provides a structured journey from learning and practice through to increasingly sophisticated forms of market participation.

ONE ECOSYSTEM. MULTIPLE WAYS TO PARTICIPATE.

RIFT gives users access to a range of trading and financial tools, including:

• Demo Trading — Practice market participation using virtual capital while learning how markets, execution and platform functionality work.

• Spot Trading — Participate directly in spot markets while developing an understanding of market behaviour, patience and risk management.

• Futures Trading — Access leveraged markets with tools and functionality designed for more advanced trading strategies and risk management.

• Smart Money — Explore structured portfolio participation through features including mirror wallets and trading books, allowing users to move beyond focusing only on individual trades.

• Auto Trading Engine — Access structured automated execution through different environments designed to support systematic and repeatable participation.

• Prediction Markets — Participate in an emerging category of market infrastructure where users can trade contracts based on the probability of future events and outcomes.

• Prop Trading Infrastructure — Learn about and participate in the evolving world of proprietary trading, funded accounts, capital allocation, performance evaluation and professional risk management.

INTELLIGENT FINANCIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT is designed around the idea that the future of finance will combine human decision-making with intelligent technology.

Modern financial markets generate enormous amounts of information. Algorithms and AI systems can process data, identify patterns, monitor markets and support execution at a speed that is impossible for an individual human to replicate.

RIFT explores how these technologies can work alongside human judgement to create more structured and intelligent financial participation.

The objective is not simply to automate everything.

It is to combine people, data, technology, risk management and intelligent execution within a connected financial ecosystem.

EDUCATION AT THE CORE

RIFT places strong emphasis on education and developing a deeper understanding of financial markets.

Through the RIFT Before You Quit educational series, training sessions and community learning, participants explore subjects including:

• Trading psychology
• Risk management
• Capital preservation
• Portfolio construction
• Capital allocation
• Market structure
• Smart money concepts
• Futures and leverage
• Prediction markets
• Proprietary trading
• Behavioural finance
• Artificial intelligence
• Algorithmic execution
• Financial infrastructure
• Professional trading principles

The objective is to help participants understand not only how to participate in markets, but also why disciplined decision-making matters.

A STRUCTURED LEARNING JOURNEY

RIFT is designed to provide a progression from education and practice toward more advanced market participation:

Learn → Demo → Spot → Futures → Smart Money → Automated Execution → Professional Trading

Each stage introduces different concepts, technologies and levels of responsibility.

Rather than focusing solely on individual trades or short-term results, RIFT encourages participants to develop a broader understanding of risk, process, discipline and capital management.

NON-CUSTODIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT follows a non-custodial approach designed to give users greater control over their own funds and reduce the need to place assets into a centralized company-controlled account.

This reflects a broader movement within digital finance toward greater transparency, user control and blockchain-based infrastructure.

ACCESS FROM ANY DEVICE

RIFT is available through the web as well as its broader platform environment, making it accessible across modern computers, smartphones and other devices.

Its lightweight infrastructure is designed to make participation practical even for users with older devices, helping remove unnecessary technology barriers to accessing modern financial tools.

THE FUTURE OF FINANCIAL PARTICIPATION

Financial markets are changing rapidly.

Trading is becoming increasingly automated. Artificial intelligence is transforming data analysis. Prediction markets are creating new forms of information-based participation. Proprietary trading is expanding access to structured capital allocation models. Blockchain infrastructure is changing how digital assets can be held and transferred.

RIFT brings these developments together within one evolving ecosystem.

• Futures and leverage
• Prediction markets
• Proprietary trading
• Behavioural finance
• Artificial intelligence
• Algorithmic execution
• Financial infrastructure
• Professional trading principles

The objective is to help participants understand not only how to participate in markets, but also why disciplined decision-making matters.

A STRUCTURED LEARNING JOURNEY

RIFT is designed to provide a progression from education and practice toward more advanced market participation:

Learn → Demo → Spot → Futures → Smart Money → Automated Execution → Professional Trading

Each stage introduces different concepts, technologies and levels of responsibility.

Rather than focusing solely on individual trades or short-term results, RIFT encourages participants to develop a broader understanding of risk, process, discipline and capital management.

NON-CUSTODIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT follows a non-custodial approach designed to give users greater control over their own funds and reduce the need to place assets into a centralized company-controlled account.

This reflects a broader movement within digital finance toward greater transparency, user control and blockchain-based infrastructure.

ACCESS FROM ANY DEVICE

RIFT is available through the web as well as its broader platform environment, making it accessible across modern computers, smartphones and other devices.

Its lightweight infrastructure is designed to make participation practical even for users with older devices, helping remove unnecessary technology barriers to accessing modern financial tools.

THE FUTURE OF FINANCIAL PARTICIPATION

Financial markets are changing rapidly.

Trading is becoming increasingly automated. Artificial intelligence is transforming data analysis. Prediction markets are creating new forms of information-based participation. Proprietary trading is expanding access to structured capital allocation models. Blockchain infrastructure is changing how digital assets can be held and transferred.

RIFT brings these developments together within one evolving ecosystem.

RIFT — THE NEXT-GEN AFFILIATE OS

Learn. Participate. Manage Risk. Think Bigger.

videos.title: The Most Critical Move for Deceptive Hockey Players
videos.summary_source_text:
The Most Critical Move for Deceptive Hockey Players The Downhill Skating System is the mechanics-first approach that unlocks effortless, controlled speed on the ice without extra conditioning, pushing or “trying harder.” Inspired by the movement signatures of players like Connor McDavid, Nathan MacKinnon, Cale Makar, Quinn Hughes, and other elite NHL skaters, this system teaches you how to move on the ice with gravity, using your body's own stretch shortening cycles mixed with the most efficient footwork patterns and various skating mechanics.

Most players skate “uphill”: stiff, blocky, pushing hard, creating tension and burning energy like we were always taught in traditional powerskating. Downhill skating flips that model. By using counter rotation, proper joint angles, and natural gravitational momentum, we teach you move faster with less effort.

Inside the Downhill Skating System, players learn to:

1) Unlock the inner spring for better acceleration.
2)Use different footwork patterns to add options, deception and effortlessness. 
3)Proper joint alignment for efficiency and balance instead of creating tension with push strides.

Apply NHL-base mechanics like shin angle, Y-angle, rhythm and cadence. Generate speed using the rocker, with heel pressure and subtle weight transfers.

This system is not what players would learn in traditional, outdated power skating methods. It’s a biomechanics-based operating system designed to match your body type and natural movement patterns.

Whether you’re trying to improve the forward stride, lateral movements, deception, or posture, Downhill Skating reveals the hidden mechanics the NHL’s best rely on, and shows you how to plug them into your game step by step.

If you’re ready to skate faster with less effort, flow through transitions, and move with the smoothness of the world’s best players, the Downhill Skating System is your blueprint to faster player development.

videos.title: The United States wins its 11th-straight Presidents Cup! |  Full Tournament Highlights | 2026
videos.summary_source_text:
The United States wins its 11th-straight Presidents Cup! |  Full Tournament Highlights | 2026 Relive all the best moments from the U.S. Team over all four days of the 2026 Presidents Cup, featuring Scottie Scheffler, Jackson Koivun, Collin Morikawa and more! 

The Presidents Cup heads to the iconic Medinah Country Club for its 16th edition, with the International Team looking to end the U.S. dominance on home soil. Scottie Scheffler headlines the American side alongside Cameron Young, Wyndham Clark, Sam Burns, Xander Schauffele and Justin Thomas, while the Internationals are led by Adam Scott, making his record-equalling 12th Presidents Cup appearance, alongside Hideki Matsuyama, Si Woo Kim and Open Champion Ryan Fox. Medinah’s newly transformed Course No. 3 provides a fresh test at 7,548 yards, with Geoff Ogilvy returning as International captain after helping oversee the redesign. The U.S. are seeking an 11th consecutive Presidents Cup victory, while the Internationals aim to claim their first win since 1998. Who do you think will come out on top at this year’s Presidents Cup?

Why? Because fixing your club path is only half the equation.

If the clubface stays open relative to that path, the ball can start right and curve even farther right.

The goal isn’t just to swing from the inside it’s to match your clubface to your path through impact.

That’s where the Blue Brick can help. It gives you a clear visual reference for your swing direction, helping you build an inside path you can repeat while learning to deliver the club more consistently. Instead of guessing what your club is doing, you can see it and train it.

videos.title: PEANUT BUTTER DOES WHAT?! Eat This and Watch What Happens | Dr. Mandell
videos.summary_source_text:
PEANUT BUTTER DOES WHAT?! Eat This and Watch What Happens | Dr. Mandell Peanut butter has been misunderstood for years. Because it’s rich, calorie-dense, and contains fat, many people automatically assume it’s a food they should avoid—especially when they’re trying to manage their weight or improve their metabolic health. But what matters isn’t simply whether a food contains fat; it’s the overall nutritional package and how it fits into your diet. Natural peanut butter provides predominantly unsaturated fats along with plant protein, fiber, magnesium, vitamin E, niacin, and other beneficial nutrients and plant compounds. That combination of fat, protein, and fiber can help slow digestion, increase fullness, and make a meal or snack more satisfying, which may help reduce the urge to keep reaching for highly refined foods between meals. Peanut butter can also change the way carbohydrates affect you when the foods are eaten together because adding fat, protein, and fiber to a carbohydrate-containing meal can slow digestion and moderate the rise in blood glucose compared with eating the carbohydrate by itself. Peanuts and other nuts have also been extensively studied as part of dietary patterns associated with cardiovascular and metabolic health, and replacing foods high in saturated fat with foods containing more unsaturated fats can help support healthier cholesterol levels. Peanut butter also provides fiber that contributes to digestive health and regularity, while its nutrient density makes a relatively small serving surprisingly satisfying. The important part is choosing a peanut butter that is primarily peanuts—ideally without large amounts of added sugar or hydrogenated fats—and remembering that portion size still matters because peanut butter is calorie-dense. Try a spoonful with an apple, celery, oatmeal, or a smoothie, or simply enjoy it by itself. And these principles aren’t limited to peanut butter; almond butter and other minimally processed nut butters can provide many of the same nutritional advantages. Healthy eating isn’t about fearing fat or labeling one food as magical—it’s about choosing nutrient-dense foods that help you stay satisfied and make your overall diet easier to maintain. If you’ve been avoiding peanut butter because you thought it was automatically “fattening,” this video may completely change the way you look at that spoonful.

***********************************

Please share this video with your friends and family.  Wishing you and your family many Blessings!  ❤️😊🙏 Dr M

videos.summary_source_text:
Small Knee Bends, Quick Steps, Just Enough To Make Them Bite The Downhill Skating System is the mechanics-first approach that unlocks effortless, controlled speed on the ice without extra conditioning, pushing or “trying harder.” Inspired by the movement signatures of players like Connor McDavid, Nathan MacKinnon, Cale Makar, Quinn Hughes, and other elite NHL skaters, this system teaches you how to move on the ice with gravity, using your body's own stretch shortening cycles mixed with the most efficient footwork patterns and various skating mechanics.

Most players skate “uphill”: stiff, blocky, pushing hard, creating tension and burning energy like we were always taught in traditional powerskating. Downhill skating flips that model. By using counter rotation, proper joint angles, and natural gravitational momentum, we teach you move faster with less effort.

Inside the Downhill Skating System, players learn to:

1) Unlock the inner spring for better acceleration.
2)Use different footwork patterns to add options, deception and effortlessness. 
3)Proper joint alignment for efficiency and balance instead of creating tension with push strides.

Apply NHL-base mechanics like shin angle, Y-angle, rhythm and cadence. Generate speed using the rocker, with heel pressure and subtle weight transfers.

This system is not what players would learn in traditional, outdated power skating methods. It’s a biomechanics-based operating system designed to match your body type and natural movement patterns.

Whether you’re trying to improve the forward stride, lateral movements, deception, or posture, Downhill Skating reveals the hidden mechanics the NHL’s best rely on, and shows you how to plug them into your game step by step.

If you’re ready to skate faster with less effort, flow through transitions, and move with the smoothness of the world’s best players, the Downhill Skating System is your blueprint to faster player development.

I Tested TWO of Golf's FASTEST Drivers…Here's What I Found Looking for the best golf driver of 2026? In this Callaway Quantum vs Titleist GTS3 driver comparison, Mark Crossfield puts two of the fastest new golf drivers head-to-head to discover how they compare and which one could be right for your golf game.

The new Callaway Quantum Triple Diamond Max and Titleist GTS3 driver promise impressive ball speeds, distance and performance. But which driver delivers the best combination of speed, forgiveness, consistency and control?

In this driver comparison video, Mark conducts a full Callaway Quantum Triple Diamond Max driver review and Titleist GTS3 driver review, comparing their technology, appearance, sound, feel and adjustability before putting both drivers through extensive testing.

Discover how the Callaway's AI-optimised face, adjustable perimeter weighting and carbon construction compare with the Titleist's Speed Synced Face, SureFit CG weighting system and aerodynamic design.

Using launch monitor data, Mark compares driver ball speed, carry distance, launch conditions and spin rates to establish whether either driver delivers a meaningful performance advantage. He also explores how each driver's weighting system and natural shot shape could influence your performance.

But launch monitor numbers only tell part of the story. Mark takes both drivers onto the golf course to see how their performance translates into real playing conditions, testing their consistency, shot-shaping capabilities, sound and feel.

With both drivers producing exceptional ball speeds and remarkably similar distances, choosing between the Callaway Quantum Triple Diamond Max and Titleist GTS3 might come down to more than simply hitting the longest drives.

Mark also compares the Callaway Quantum prices with the Titleist GTS 3 prices, and explains which driver he would personally choose, considering everything from performance and adjustability to appearance, sound and feel.

If you're considering buying a new golf driver in 2026, wondering whether the Callaway Quantum or Titleist GTS3 is worth your money, or simply want to see how two of golf's biggest manufacturers compare, this comprehensive driver test should help you understand what each model has to offer.

I gave my Claude AI trading bot $100 and one challenge: double the account in 22 hours.

Could an AI trading bot discover its own strategies, test them and trade real money successfully?

Instead of asking Claude to predict the entire market, I gave it one specific task: predict whether the next 15-minute candle would finish higher or lower.

But there was a problem. Winning trades paid less than losing trades cost. Once fees were included, a 50% win rate would lose money.

So before risking the $100, I gave Claude two hours to research and backtest strategies using TradingKit. It tested over 1,600 strategies across more than 34,000 variants, narrowed them down through validation and selected five for live trading.

Then we hit another obstacle: the broker’s up-or-down product had no API available for this setup. Claude built a Chrome extension to automate the trades through my browser.

🌟 Take the 2-minute Health Lever Quiz: https://drbrg.co/4ruU5V6

Common signs of nutritional deficiencies include:
• Pale skin — Vitamin B12
• Cracking at the corners of the mouth — Vitamin B2
• Ridges on the fingernails — Iron
• White spots on the nails — Zinc
• Bleeding gums — Vitamin C
• Thinning outer eyebrows — Iodine
• Restless legs at night — Magnesium
• Calf cramps — Magnesium
• Thinning hair — Biotin
• Cold hands and feet — Vitamin B12
• Dark circles under the eyes — Iron or Vitamin K
• Craving ice — Iron

Matt Fitzpatrick’s Final 9 Holes in France | Every Shot Watch the Back 9 on Sunday, presented by Nexo, as Matt Fitzpatrick secured a three-shot victory at the 2026 FedEx Open de France to claim his 11th DP World Tour win and first FedEx Open de France title. 

► SUBSCRIBE: http://et.golf/Subscribe 

Michael Kim returns as defending champion to play in Europe for the first time since July, but this time he’ll be playing at a completely different course. He is joined by a field headlined by Ryder Cup stars such as Tommy Fleetwood, Matt Fitzpatrick, Ludvig Åberg, and Viktor Hovland who all arrive after competing at the BMW PGA Championship. They are joined by PGA Tour winners Kristoffer Reitan, Ryan Gerard and Cameron Smith. A strong home contingent featuring Matthieu Pavon and Adrien Saddier rounds off a phenomenal line-up. videos.title: Has George Cracked The Code? | Azerbaijan GP Review | F1 Nation Podcast
videos.summary_source_text:
Has George Cracked The Code? | Azerbaijan GP Review | F1 Nation Podcast Tom Clarkson, James Hinchcliffe and Alex Brundle sit down in the Baku paddock to dissect a thrilling Azerbaijan Grand Prix.

George Russell may have only won the race by a tenth after a dramatic drag race with Max Verstappen to the finish line, but he was dominant all weekend to take his third victory of the season.

Why was George back to his best in Baku? Has he finally got to grips with the car? And what does this result mean for his title challenge?

Kimi Antonelli recovered from his crash in qualifying to climb from P16 to P5. Given the Mercedes’ straight-line speed, why wasn’t he able to cut through the field as successfully as he did in Monza? And was this the first time we’ve seen Kimi race with the championship in mind?

The guys also discuss Red Bull's first double podium since China 2024 - whether Max could have won had he qualified higher up, the team orders between him and Isack Hadjar, and just how impressive the latter’s performance was after missing the previous three races with a wrist injury.

Elsewhere, there was mayhem in the midfield as Franco Colapinto took out Alpine teammate Pierre Gasly and McLaren’s Lando Norris at the first Safety Car restart, when Arvid Lindblad also hit his Racing Bulls teammate Liam Lawson. So what will the debriefs at Alpine and Racing Bulls look like?

Also on the agenda: Esteban Ocon’s future after leading Haas to a double points finish, a much-needed point for Williams, disappointment for Oscar Piastri having been in podium contention and an anonymous race for Ferrari.

Explore new and used car deals with Carwow: https://bit.ly/Change-Your-Car-28-09-26

Who’s ready for an American vs Japan showdown?! 

We’ve got our hands on a 4th generation Dodge Viper ACR, and it’s lining up against the legendary Lexus LFA! 

The question is, which V10 will make it to the finish line first? Let’s take a closer look at the stats…

First up we have the Dodge Viper ACR. It’s powered by an 8.4-litre naturally aspirated V10 which produces 608hp and 760Nm. However, it’s had a slight tune applied to it, meaning the output is more likely to be around 650hp and 800Nm! All of this power is sent to the rear wheels via a 6-speed manual, and it tips the scales at 1,533kg. As of today, it’s valued at around £130,000.  

Next up, we have the Lexus LFA. It’s powered by a 4.8-litre naturally aspirated V10, and this creates 560hp and 480Nm. Power is sent to the rear wheels only via a 6-speed auto gearbox, and the car tips the scales at 1,480kg. As new, it cost around £336,000, but as of today, it’s valued at around £750,000.

videos.title: Jon Machota: Cowboys Had the Game Won — Then Blew It
videos.summary_source_text:
Jon Machota: Cowboys Had the Game Won — Then Blew It The Cowboys had a chance to win in Brazil — and Clarence Hill and The Athletic's Jon Machota aren't letting them off the hook.

After Dallas' 34–31 loss to the Ravens, Clarence and Jon break down a brutal finish that saw the Cowboys fail to capitalize late. They discuss the final drive, Dak Prescott's decision-making, the Cowboys' offensive stars, the defense's final stand and the coaching decisions that helped turn a potential victory into an overtime loss.

They also look ahead to a brutal short week against the Houston Texans and the Cowboys' 1–2 start.

Plus: Why this loss felt particularly frustrating, and why Jon says this was as angry and frustrated as he's seen Dak Prescott after a regular-season game.

Cowboys 31, Ravens 34. Dallas heads to Houston.

videos.summary_source_text:
The Main Difference Between Hockey and Basketball The Downhill Skating System is the mechanics-first approach that unlocks effortless, controlled speed on the ice without extra conditioning, pushing or “trying harder.” Inspired by the movement signatures of players like Connor McDavid, Nathan MacKinnon, Cale Makar, Quinn Hughes, and other elite NHL skaters, this system teaches you how to move on the ice with gravity, using your body's own stretch shortening cycles mixed with the most efficient footwork patterns and various skating mechanics.

Most players skate “uphill”: stiff, blocky, pushing hard, creating tension and burning energy like we were always taught in traditional powerskating. Downhill skating flips that model. By using counter rotation, proper joint angles, and natural gravitational momentum, we teach you move faster with less effort.

Inside the Downhill Skating System, players learn to:

1) Unlock the inner spring for better acceleration.
2)Use different footwork patterns to add options, deception and effortlessness. 
3)Proper joint alignment for efficiency and balance instead of creating tension with push strides.

Apply NHL-base mechanics like shin angle, Y-angle, rhythm and cadence. Generate speed using the rocker, with heel pressure and subtle weight transfers.

This system is not what players would learn in traditional, outdated power skating methods. It’s a biomechanics-based operating system designed to match your body type and natural movement patterns.

Whether you’re trying to improve the forward stride, lateral movements, deception, or posture, Downhill Skating reveals the hidden mechanics the NHL’s best rely on, and shows you how to plug them into your game step by step.

If you’re ready to skate faster with less effort, flow through transitions, and move with the smoothness of the world’s best players, the Downhill Skating System is your blueprint to faster player development.

videos.title: Numbness, Tingling & Burning? These 7 Nutrients Can Help Your Nerves | Dr. Mandell
videos.summary_source_text:
Numbness, Tingling & Burning? These 7 Nutrients Can Help Your Nerves | Dr. Mandell If you’re experiencing numbness, tingling, burning, stabbing sensations, or other symptoms associated with irritated or damaged nerves, there are important nutrients that play roles in normal nerve and nervous-system function. In this video, Dr. Alan Mandell explains several nutritional compounds associated with nerve health, inflammation, metabolic health, and healthy nerve signaling. Neuropathy can have many different causes, including diabetes, nutritional deficiencies, medication effects, alcohol use, injury, and certain medical conditions, so understanding and addressing the underlying cause is extremely important. Supporting your body with proper nutrition may be an important part of maintaining healthy nerves and normal nerve function. Persistent, unexplained, or worsening numbness, weakness, burning, or pain should always be properly evaluated. 

THE 7 NERVE-SUPPORTING NUTRIENTS & COMPOUNDS DISCUSSED:

Turmeric / Curcumin — Antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties; black pepper (piperine) can substantially increase curcumin absorption.
B Vitamins (B1, B6 & B12) — Important for normal nerve and nervous-system function. B12 deficiency can cause neurological symptoms; excessive supplemental B6 can also damage nerves.
Omega-3 Fatty Acids — EPA and DHA provide important structural fats used by cells throughout the body, including the nervous system.
Vitamin D — Important for normal immune, muscle, bone, and nervous-system function.
Apple Cider Vinegar — Discussed in the video primarily in relation to blood-sugar and metabolic health rather than as a direct treatment for neuropathy.
Alpha-Lipoic Acid (ALA) — An antioxidant that has been studied particularly for symptoms associated with diabetic peripheral neuropathy.
Magnesium — Important for normal nerve and muscle function and involved in hundreds of biochemical reactions throughout the body.

***********************************

videos.title: Google's Gemini Notebook Is Becoming an AI Research Workspace
videos.summary_source_text:
Google's Gemini Notebook Is Becoming an AI Research Workspace https://bitbiased.ai/ai-automation-services

Google renamed NotebookLM to Gemini Notebook — but the rebrand is the least interesting part. The bigger change is that every notebook can now come with what Google calls a “secure cloud computer,” allowing Gemini to write and execute Python code against your own documents instead of simply summarizing them.

That pushes Gemini Notebook much closer to a full research platform. It can answer questions from source material with clickable citations, generate podcast-style Audio Overviews, create narrated slide videos, build quizzes and flashcards, analyze data with Python, and even pull eligible Google Play ebooks you own directly into a notebook.

But there are some important catches.

Gemini Notebook is still source-grounded, not automatically fact-checked. A citation proves where an answer came from — it doesn’t prove the answer is correct. Conflicting sources can still cause problems, scanned PDFs and poor transcripts can contaminate everything built from them, and Google itself says users should verify generated answers against the original material.

The new cloud computer is arguably the biggest technical leap. Gemini can extract information from documents, write Python, execute calculations, and return tables or charts. That puts it in territory already familiar to users of ChatGPT’s Code Interpreter. However, the feature initially arrived for Google AI Ultra and Workspace Ultra users, only Python executes automatically, and questions remain around exactly how persistent these compute environments are.

Then there’s the multimedia side. Audio Overviews turn research into AI-hosted podcast conversations, while interactive voice lets you interrupt and ask questions. Video Overviews create narrated slide presentations, and Short Video Overviews compress individual ideas into roughly 60-second vertical explainers. These aren’t AI-generated movies — they’re closer to automatically assembled presentations.

Gemini Notebook is also becoming a serious study tool, with flashcards, quizzes, mind maps, study guides, and Google’s LearnLM technology sitting behind parts of the education experience.

And Google is expanding what counts as a “source.” Expert Intelligence lets users import eligible Google Play ebooks they already own, with Google saying more than 100,000 titles were supported at launch. Instead of relying on what an AI model remembers about a book, Gemini Notebook can work directly from the purchased text.

That matters because this increasingly looks like an ecosystem play. Notebook content already connects with Gemini, while Google has said integration with Search’s AI Mode is coming. Combine that with Gemini appearing across Gmail and Docs, and your notebooks could become a persistent context layer across more of Google’s products.

Google says Gemini Notebook has passed 30 million users and 600,000 organizations, but the practical limitations still matter. Usage is constrained by compute quotas, demanding features like audio and video consume that budget faster, and free notebooks have source limits. Paid plans range from AI Plus and AI Pro through AI Ultra, with higher tiers getting larger quotas and earlier access to advanced features.

So what actually changed when NotebookLM became Gemini Notebook? We break down the cloud computer, source grounding, Audio and Video Overviews, Expert Intelligence, pricing and limits, Google’s wider ecosystem strategy, and where Gemini Notebook still falls short compared with tools like ChatGPT and Claude.

01:35 Where Gemini Notebook Came From
02:45 What You Can Actually Feed It
03:23 What Source-Grounded Actually Means
04:24 The Actual Leap: A Cloud Computer
05:55 Notebooks You Can Listen To — and Now Talk To
06:50 Slide Videos, Not Movies
07:31 It Also Wants to Be Your Study App
08:51 Expert Intelligence: Pulling Real Books

12:20 The Verdict

videos.summary_source_text:
If You Never Learned This, You Were Taught To Protect The Puck The Slow Way The Downhill Skating System is the mechanics-first approach that unlocks effortless, controlled speed on the ice without extra conditioning, pushing or “trying harder.” Inspired by the movement signatures of players like Connor McDavid, Nathan MacKinnon, Cale Makar, Quinn Hughes, and other elite NHL skaters, this system teaches you how to move on the ice with gravity, using your body's own stretch shortening cycles mixed with the most efficient footwork patterns and various skating mechanics.

Most players skate “uphill”: stiff, blocky, pushing hard, creating tension and burning energy like we were always taught in traditional powerskating. Downhill skating flips that model. By using counter rotation, proper joint angles, and natural gravitational momentum, we teach you move faster with less effort.

Inside the Downhill Skating System, players learn to:

1) Unlock the inner spring for better acceleration.
2)Use different footwork patterns to add options, deception and effortlessness. 
3)Proper joint alignment for efficiency and balance instead of creating tension with push strides.

Apply NHL-base mechanics like shin angle, Y-angle, rhythm and cadence. Generate speed using the rocker, with heel pressure and subtle weight transfers.

This system is not what players would learn in traditional, outdated power skating methods. It’s a biomechanics-based operating system designed to match your body type and natural movement patterns.

Whether you’re trying to improve the forward stride, lateral movements, deception, or posture, Downhill Skating reveals the hidden mechanics the NHL’s best rely on, and shows you how to plug them into your game step by step.

If you’re ready to skate faster with less effort, flow through transitions, and move with the smoothness of the world’s best players, the Downhill Skating System is your blueprint to faster player development.

Learn about common acid reflux drugs and their side effects, plus the underlying acid reflux causes most people don’t know about.

In a clinical trial involving 120 healthy people, participants were given omeprazole. None had heartburn or acid reflux at the start of the trial, yet afterward, nearly half developed heartburn, indigestion, or acid reflux.

Acid reflux isn’t always a problem of too much stomach acid. In fact, many people with GERD and acid reflux may actually have low stomach acid.

Antacids aren’t meant to be taken long term; however, many people use them for extended periods. Side effects associated with long-term use can include nutritional deficiencies, anxiety, depression, and more.

Overeating, a hiatal hernia, and high-sugar diets can also contribute to heartburn and acid reflux.

Betaine hydrochloride can help acidify the stomach and may help reduce GERD symptoms. Zinc carnosine can also support digestive health if you’re dealing with an ulcer or stomach inflammation.

Place an alignment stick behind the ball and a head cover just in front — then focus on swinging under the stick and over the head cover. 
You’ll shallow the club naturally, improve your path, and start hitting up on the ball for better launch and distance.

Stop Doing C-Cuts Skate Like This Instead The Downhill Skating System is the mechanics-first approach that unlocks effortless, controlled speed on the ice without extra conditioning, pushing or “trying harder.” Inspired by the movement signatures of players like Connor McDavid, Nathan MacKinnon, Cale Makar, Quinn Hughes, and other elite NHL skaters, this system teaches you how to move on the ice with gravity, using your body's own stretch shortening cycles mixed with the most efficient footwork patterns and various skating mechanics.

Most players skate “uphill”: stiff, blocky, pushing hard, creating tension and burning energy like we were always taught in traditional powerskating. Downhill skating flips that model. By using counter rotation, proper joint angles, and natural gravitational momentum, we teach you move faster with less effort.

Inside the Downhill Skating System, players learn to:

1) Unlock the inner spring for better acceleration.
2)Use different footwork patterns to add options, deception and effortlessness. 
3)Proper joint alignment for efficiency and balance instead of creating tension with push strides.

Apply NHL-base mechanics like shin angle, Y-angle, rhythm and cadence. Generate speed using the rocker, with heel pressure and subtle weight transfers.

This system is not what players would learn in traditional, outdated power skating methods. It’s a biomechanics-based operating system designed to match your body type and natural movement patterns.

Whether you’re trying to improve the forward stride, lateral movements, deception, or posture, Downhill Skating reveals the hidden mechanics the NHL’s best rely on, and shows you how to plug them into your game step by step.

If you’re ready to skate faster with less effort, flow through transitions, and move with the smoothness of the world’s best players, the Downhill Skating System is your blueprint to faster player development.

videos.summary_source_text:
Belly Fat Won’t Go Away? Do These 6 Things | Dr. Mandell If stubborn belly fat just doesn’t seem to go away despite your best efforts, there may be more to consider than simply doing more crunches or adding more cardio. In this video, Dr. Alan Mandell explains six important lifestyle and nutrition changes that can help create a healthier environment for your body to access stored fat. You’ll learn why giving your body adequate time between meals can allow insulin levels to come down, how starting meals with protein and soluble fiber can slow digestion and help control blood sugar and appetite, and why foods such as oats, chia seeds, flax seeds, psyllium, lentils, beans, and certain fruits can benefit both metabolic health and your gut microbiome. We’ll also discuss why frequently drinking sugary carbohydrates can work against your goals, how quality sleep influences insulin sensitivity and stress hormones, and why managing chronic stress is an important part of the picture. Belly fat cannot simply be spot-reduced with abdominal exercises, so the goal is to address the everyday signals that influence appetite, energy storage, and fat metabolism throughout your entire body. These six changes aren’t about starving yourself or spending endless hours exercising—they’re about understanding how your body responds to food, sleep, stress, and daily habits and then using that knowledge to make better choices consistently. Give your body the right signals, stay consistent, and allow those small changes to compound over time.
