videos.title: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash Is a Freak: 552B Parameters, Only 8B Active
videos.summary_source_text:
DeepSeek V4.1 Flash Is a Freak: 552B Parameters, Only 8B Active https://bitbiased.ai/ai-automation-services

DeepSeek says V4.1-Flash scored 90.6 on Terminal-Bench 2.1, ahead of Claude Opus 5 at 89.1 and GPT-5.6 Sol at 88.8. Even more striking: this is a 552-billion-parameter model that activates just 8 billion parameters per input token.

But that headline needs context.

DeepSeek V4.1-Flash arrived on September 10 with open weights under an MIT license, native vision, a one-million-token context window, and an architecture designed around a simple reality of AI agents: they spend far more tokens reading than writing. DeepSeek's answer is to make that reading dramatically cheaper.

One real-world test shows why this matters. DataCamp gave V4.1-Flash a screenshot of a broken Flask dashboard and access to the underlying project. Without being told where the bugs were, the agent identified problems across Python, CSS, and JavaScript and produced a three-file patch. All five tests passed.

Then there was a problem: the webpage was still wrong.

The agent correctly diagnosed that the Flask server was running stale code, but it had no tool to restart it before hitting its turn limit. A human restart was required. It's a useful example of the difference between fixing code and actually completing an autonomous software task.

The entire run involved 156,724 input tokens, with an 87% cache hit rate, plus 11,497 output tokens. Reported off-peak cost: about one cent.

That efficiency comes from some unusual architecture. V4.1-Flash combines mixture-of-experts routing with a split encoder-decoder design. DeepSeek says only 8 billion parameters are active per token during input processing and 16 billion during generation. Its KV cache is also just 890 bytes per token, using compressed sparse attention, 4-bit cache storage, and on-demand reconstruction.

At DeepSeek's off-peak pricing, cached input costs $0.003 per million tokens. That sounds almost absurdly cheap—but price per token isn't necessarily price per completed task.

So we go through DeepSeek's benchmark table line by line.

V4.1-Flash scores 90.6 on Terminal-Bench 2.1, 74.2 on DeepSWE, 88.1 on CyberGym, and 54.8 on AutomationBench. But harder benchmarks tell a different story. On Terminal-Bench 3.0 it scores 30.0 versus 43.3 for Claude Opus 5, while Terminal-Bench 4.0 shows 31.2 versus 51.8. DeepSeek's own results also show that changing the agent harness can move its DeepSWE score from 65.5 to 74.2.

Then there's the competition DeepSeek's original chart didn't include. Around the same period, newer models arrived from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and xAI, including GPT-6 Luna, GPT-6 Sol, Claude Opus 5.5, Gemini 3.8 Flash, and Grok 4.7. That changes how V4.1-Flash's headline comparisons should be interpreted.

Independent Artificial Analysis testing adds another piece: V4.1-Flash scored 39 on its Intelligence Index versus 36 for V4-Pro and reached roughly 227 tokens per second. But it also generated substantially more output tokens than the median comparable model, pushing its measured cost per task to $0.27.

So is DeepSeek V4.1-Flash actually a frontier-model killer, or is its real achievement something more interesting: making long-context, input-heavy AI agents dramatically cheaper to run?

We break down the architecture, pricing, benchmarks, independent testing, limitations, and what DeepSeek's upcoming V4.1-Pro could mean next. :contentReference[oaicite:0]{index=0}

videos.title: “Fable 5.2” Just DESTROYED GPT-6 Astra
videos.summary_source_text:
“Fable 5.2” Just DESTROYED GPT-6 Astra https://bitbiased.ai/ai-automation-services

A supposed “Fable 5.2” is being credited with beating GPT-6 Astra, quietly appearing inside Claude Code, and delivering major coding and visual-generation upgrades. But there’s one problem: Anthropic has never announced a model called Fable 5.2.

As of September 21st, Anthropic’s official page still lists Claude Fable 5.1 as its most capable model for ambitious coding projects. There’s no Fable 5.2 model ID, pricing page, system card, benchmark table, or launch announcement.

So where did the rumor come from — and is there actually a secret Anthropic model being tested?

The trail starts on September 1st, when investor Gavin Baker speculated that Anthropic might already have “Fable 5.2” ready. After OpenAI released GPT-6 Astra on September 3rd, that speculation accelerated. Within days, social-media posts were claiming Anthropic’s next Fable could come from an entirely new pretraining run and arrive by late September or early October.

Then users began claiming they were actually encountering the mystery model inside Claude Code.

Some testers reported that Fable 5.1 sessions appeared to be routing to a “next Fable” model. One unusual test involved asking Claude about “Tibo the reset guy,” with users treating knowledge of that recent niche reference as evidence that they had reached a newer checkpoint.

But that test has a major problem: getting the answer right doesn’t reveal which model produced it. Different post-training data, hidden context, memory, retrieval, A/B testing, effort settings, or another checkpoint could potentially produce the same result.

Anthropic does officially document model routing in certain circumstances, so the underlying infrastructure exists. What hasn’t surfaced is an API model identifier, network artifact, billing identifier, leaked system card, or other technical evidence proving regular users are secretly being routed to “Fable 5.2.”

The viral demos have similar limitations. One Reddit user reported that a suspected newer model made real progress on coding projects where Fable 5.1 had struggled, including choosing a state-machine architecture for a Rust networking protocol. A September 19th visual comparison also appeared to show the mystery model going head-to-head with GPT-6 Astra.

Interesting evidence — but neither confirms the backend model.

There’s another complication: Fable 5.1 is already extremely capable. Anthropic says it has a 1-million-token context window, up to 128,000 output tokens, adaptive thinking, and substantial improvements across coding, terminal, browser-agent, and knowledge-work tasks. Different effort settings alone can also produce noticeable changes in quality, speed, and cost.

That means an impressive coding result, frontend demo, game, SVG, or 3D generation isn't automatically evidence of a secret model.

Then Reuters added the strongest evidence yet. On September 19th, Reuters reported, citing three sources, that Anthropic was considering rolling out a new AI model, with one source saying it was undergoing safety evaluation.

That matters — but Reuters did NOT call it Fable 5.2, did not report that it came from a new pretraining run, and did not provide a release date.

So this investigation separates what we can actually substantiate from what the internet has gradually converted into “fact”: the origins of the Fable 5.2 name, the alleged new pretraining run, Claude Code routing reports, the viral Astra comparisons, what Fable 5.1 can already do, the Reuters report, and the alternative explanations that could account for the mystery-model sightings.

Something new may genuinely be under evaluation at Anthropic. The much bigger question is what that model actually is.

A Confident Saucer Breaks Systems Faster Than Any Deke The Downhill Skating System is the mechanics-first approach that unlocks effortless, controlled speed on the ice without extra conditioning, pushing or “trying harder.” Inspired by the movement signatures of players like Connor McDavid, Nathan MacKinnon, Cale Makar, Quinn Hughes, and other elite NHL skaters, this system teaches you how to move on the ice with gravity, using your body's own stretch shortening cycles mixed with the most efficient footwork patterns and various skating mechanics.

Most players skate “uphill”: stiff, blocky, pushing hard, creating tension and burning energy like we were always taught in traditional powerskating. Downhill skating flips that model. By using counter rotation, proper joint angles, and natural gravitational momentum, we teach you move faster with less effort.

Inside the Downhill Skating System, players learn to:

1) Unlock the inner spring for better acceleration.
2)Use different footwork patterns to add options, deception and effortlessness. 
3)Proper joint alignment for efficiency and balance instead of creating tension with push strides.

Apply NHL-base mechanics like shin angle, Y-angle, rhythm and cadence. Generate speed using the rocker, with heel pressure and subtle weight transfers.

This system is not what players would learn in traditional, outdated power skating methods. It’s a biomechanics-based operating system designed to match your body type and natural movement patterns.

Whether you’re trying to improve the forward stride, lateral movements, deception, or posture, Downhill Skating reveals the hidden mechanics the NHL’s best rely on, and shows you how to plug them into your game step by step.

If you’re ready to skate faster with less effort, flow through transitions, and move with the smoothness of the world’s best players, the Downhill Skating System is your blueprint to faster player development.

videos.summary_source_text:
Before Hitting Your Woods - Make This 5 Second Change Fairway woods and hybrids should make golf easier… but for a lot of golfers they’re some of the hardest clubs in the bag to hit consistently.

Tops, thin shots, heavy strikes and weak shots to the right can quickly destroy your confidence.

And according to Shot Scope, the average golfer uses a fairway wood or hybrid for around 25% of their shots — so learning how to strike them properly can make a huge difference to your scores.

In this golf lesson, Danny Maude shows you two simple drills to help you hit your fairway woods and hybrids cleaner, straighter and with more distance.

The first drill helps you improve your ball striking and understand how the club should travel through impact.

The second helps you create more speed and naturally square the clubface — without trying to manipulate your golf swing.

If you struggle to hit fairway woods off the ground, top your 3 wood, thin your hybrids or slice them to the right, this lesson should really help.

You’ll discover:

• Why golfers top fairway woods and hybrids  
• Why thin shots can happen for a completely different reason  
• The ideal strike for a fairway wood off the ground  
• A simple finish position that can improve your contact  
• Why the trail shoulder matters through impact  
• How to create a shallow, sweeping strike with fairway woods  
• The ball position I recommend for a fairway wood  
• A simple drill you can use before you play  
• Why forcing positions can make your swing feel wooden  
• How opening the clubface can actually help a golfer who slices  
• How to square the clubface naturally through impact  
• Why releasing the club can create more speed and distance  
• How to hit fairway woods with a powerful sweeping motion  
• How to know whether you are too steep or leaning back in your golf swing  

One of the biggest mistakes golfers make with fairway woods is trying to lift the golf ball into the air.

The club already has loft.

Your job is to create a strike where the club travels beautifully through the ball and brushes the turf — allowing the loft of the club to launch the golf ball for you.

Once you understand that sensation, fairway woods and hybrids can start to feel dramatically easier.

videos.summary_source_text:
25.09.26 - RIFT Education Day RIFT is a modern, non-custodial trading and financial technology ecosystem designed to bring together market access, education, intelligent execution, portfolio participation and professional trading infrastructure in one connected environment.

Built for both newcomers and experienced market participants, RIFT provides a structured journey from learning and practice through to increasingly sophisticated forms of market participation.

ONE ECOSYSTEM. MULTIPLE WAYS TO PARTICIPATE.

RIFT gives users access to a range of trading and financial tools, including:

• Demo Trading — Practice market participation using virtual capital while learning how markets, execution and platform functionality work.

• Spot Trading — Participate directly in spot markets while developing an understanding of market behaviour, patience and risk management.

• Futures Trading — Access leveraged markets with tools and functionality designed for more advanced trading strategies and risk management.

• Smart Money — Explore structured portfolio participation through features including mirror wallets and trading books, allowing users to move beyond focusing only on individual trades.

• Auto Trading Engine — Access structured automated execution through different environments designed to support systematic and repeatable participation.

• Prediction Markets — Participate in an emerging category of market infrastructure where users can trade contracts based on the probability of future events and outcomes.

• Prop Trading Infrastructure — Learn about and participate in the evolving world of proprietary trading, funded accounts, capital allocation, performance evaluation and professional risk management.

INTELLIGENT FINANCIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT is designed around the idea that the future of finance will combine human decision-making with intelligent technology.

Modern financial markets generate enormous amounts of information. Algorithms and AI systems can process data, identify patterns, monitor markets and support execution at a speed that is impossible for an individual human to replicate.

RIFT explores how these technologies can work alongside human judgement to create more structured and intelligent financial participation.

The objective is not simply to automate everything.

It is to combine people, data, technology, risk management and intelligent execution within a connected financial ecosystem.

EDUCATION AT THE CORE

RIFT places strong emphasis on education and developing a deeper understanding of financial markets.

Through the RIFT Before You Quit educational series, training sessions and community learning, participants explore subjects including:

• Trading psychology
• Risk management
• Capital preservation
• Portfolio construction
• Capital allocation
• Market structure
• Smart money concepts
• Futures and leverage
• Prediction markets
• Proprietary trading
• Behavioural finance
• Artificial intelligence
• Algorithmic execution
• Financial infrastructure
• Professional trading principles

The objective is to help participants understand not only how to participate in markets, but also why disciplined decision-making matters.

A STRUCTURED LEARNING JOURNEY

RIFT is designed to provide a progression from education and practice toward more advanced market participation:

Learn → Demo → Spot → Futures → Smart Money → Automated Execution → Professional Trading

Each stage introduces different concepts, technologies and levels of responsibility.

Rather than focusing solely on individual trades or short-term results, RIFT encourages participants to develop a broader understanding of risk, process, discipline and capital management.

NON-CUSTODIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT follows a non-custodial approach designed to give users greater control over their own funds and reduce the need to place assets into a centralized company-controlled account.

This reflects a broader movement within digital finance toward greater transparency, user control and blockchain-based infrastructure.

ACCESS FROM ANY DEVICE

RIFT is available through the web as well as its broader platform environment, making it accessible across modern computers, smartphones and other devices.

Its lightweight infrastructure is designed to make participation practical even for users with older devices, helping remove unnecessary technology barriers to accessing modern financial tools.

THE FUTURE OF FINANCIAL PARTICIPATION

Financial markets are changing rapidly.

Trading is becoming increasingly automated. Artificial intelligence is transforming data analysis. Prediction markets are creating new forms of information-based participation. Proprietary trading is expanding access to structured capital allocation models. Blockchain infrastructure is changing how digital assets can be held and transferred.

RIFT brings these developments together within one evolving ecosystem.

videos.title: Hindi - 25.09.26 - RIFT Presentation
videos.summary_source_text:
Hindi - 25.09.26 - RIFT Presentation RIFT is a modern, non-custodial trading and financial technology ecosystem designed to bring together market access, education, intelligent execution, portfolio participation and professional trading infrastructure in one connected environment.

Built for both newcomers and experienced market participants, RIFT provides a structured journey from learning and practice through to increasingly sophisticated forms of market participation.

ONE ECOSYSTEM. MULTIPLE WAYS TO PARTICIPATE.

RIFT gives users access to a range of trading and financial tools, including:

• Demo Trading — Practice market participation using virtual capital while learning how markets, execution and platform functionality work.

• Spot Trading — Participate directly in spot markets while developing an understanding of market behaviour, patience and risk management.

• Futures Trading — Access leveraged markets with tools and functionality designed for more advanced trading strategies and risk management.

• Smart Money — Explore structured portfolio participation through features including mirror wallets and trading books, allowing users to move beyond focusing only on individual trades.

• Auto Trading Engine — Access structured automated execution through different environments designed to support systematic and repeatable participation.

• Prediction Markets — Participate in an emerging category of market infrastructure where users can trade contracts based on the probability of future events and outcomes.

• Prop Trading Infrastructure — Learn about and participate in the evolving world of proprietary trading, funded accounts, capital allocation, performance evaluation and professional risk management.

INTELLIGENT FINANCIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT is designed around the idea that the future of finance will combine human decision-making with intelligent technology.

Modern financial markets generate enormous amounts of information. Algorithms and AI systems can process data, identify patterns, monitor markets and support execution at a speed that is impossible for an individual human to replicate.

RIFT explores how these technologies can work alongside human judgement to create more structured and intelligent financial participation.

The objective is not simply to automate everything.

It is to combine people, data, technology, risk management and intelligent execution within a connected financial ecosystem.

EDUCATION AT THE CORE

RIFT places strong emphasis on education and developing a deeper understanding of financial markets.

Through the RIFT Before You Quit educational series, training sessions and community learning, participants explore subjects including:

• Trading psychology
• Risk management
• Capital preservation
• Portfolio construction
• Capital allocation
• Market structure
• Smart money concepts
• Futures and leverage
• Prediction markets
• Proprietary trading
• Behavioural finance
• Artificial intelligence
• Algorithmic execution
• Financial infrastructure
• Professional trading principles

The objective is to help participants understand not only how to participate in markets, but also why disciplined decision-making matters.

A STRUCTURED LEARNING JOURNEY

RIFT is designed to provide a progression from education and practice toward more advanced market participation:

Learn → Demo → Spot → Futures → Smart Money → Automated Execution → Professional Trading

Each stage introduces different concepts, technologies and levels of responsibility.

Rather than focusing solely on individual trades or short-term results, RIFT encourages participants to develop a broader understanding of risk, process, discipline and capital management.

NON-CUSTODIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT follows a non-custodial approach designed to give users greater control over their own funds and reduce the need to place assets into a centralized company-controlled account.

This reflects a broader movement within digital finance toward greater transparency, user control and blockchain-based infrastructure.

ACCESS FROM ANY DEVICE

RIFT is available through the web as well as its broader platform environment, making it accessible across modern computers, smartphones and other devices.

Its lightweight infrastructure is designed to make participation practical even for users with older devices, helping remove unnecessary technology barriers to accessing modern financial tools.

THE FUTURE OF FINANCIAL PARTICIPATION

Financial markets are changing rapidly.

Trading is becoming increasingly automated. Artificial intelligence is transforming data analysis. Prediction markets are creating new forms of information-based participation. Proprietary trading is expanding access to structured capital allocation models. Blockchain infrastructure is changing how digital assets can be held and transferred.

RIFT brings these developments together within one evolving ecosystem.

videos.summary_source_text:
No More Toe Drags The Downhill Skating System is the mechanics-first approach that unlocks effortless, controlled speed on the ice without extra conditioning, pushing or “trying harder.” Inspired by the movement signatures of players like Connor McDavid, Nathan MacKinnon, Cale Makar, Quinn Hughes, and other elite NHL skaters, this system teaches you how to move on the ice with gravity, using your body's own stretch shortening cycles mixed with the most efficient footwork patterns and various skating mechanics.

Most players skate “uphill”: stiff, blocky, pushing hard, creating tension and burning energy like we were always taught in traditional powerskating. Downhill skating flips that model. By using counter rotation, proper joint angles, and natural gravitational momentum, we teach you move faster with less effort.

Inside the Downhill Skating System, players learn to:

1) Unlock the inner spring for better acceleration.
2)Use different footwork patterns to add options, deception and effortlessness. 
3)Proper joint alignment for efficiency and balance instead of creating tension with push strides.

Apply NHL-base mechanics like shin angle, Y-angle, rhythm and cadence. Generate speed using the rocker, with heel pressure and subtle weight transfers.

This system is not what players would learn in traditional, outdated power skating methods. It’s a biomechanics-based operating system designed to match your body type and natural movement patterns.

Whether you’re trying to improve the forward stride, lateral movements, deception, or posture, Downhill Skating reveals the hidden mechanics the NHL’s best rely on, and shows you how to plug them into your game step by step.

If you’re ready to skate faster with less effort, flow through transitions, and move with the smoothness of the world’s best players, the Downhill Skating System is your blueprint to faster player development.

7 Warning Signs of a Slow Thyroid You Need to Know A slow thyroid can affect numerous aspects of your health, but many doctors miss the signs.

🌟 Take the 2-minute Health Lever Quiz: https://drbrg.co/3VpP83N

Just so you know, my full line of high-quality supplements is available on Amazon — search Dr. Berg Supplements.

Here are 7 common symptoms of hypothyroidism you may not have realized are related to your thyroid:

1. Eyebrow changes
Disappearing outer thirds of your eyebrows? Thyroid hormones power your hair follicles, so hair loss in this area can signal a thyroid issue.

2. High cholesterol levels
High cholesterol often leads to immediate medication prescriptions. But did you know a slow thyroid can cause this imbalance? Addressing it may normalize your cholesterol levels.

3. Puffy face
Waking up with facial puffiness? This could indicate your thyroid is trapping water beneath the skin, a common symptom of thyroid dysfunction.

4. Carpal tunnel syndrome
Fluid accumulation around the median nerve can be a result of hypothyroidism, and swelling can lead to carpal tunnel syndrome.

5. Mood changes
Feeling depressed or anxious? Over 50% of those with a slow thyroid experience mood disorders. Thyroid hormones are essential for energy production in your brain.

6. Persistent headaches
Thyroid issues can cause muscle tightness in your neck. This tension may lead to headaches or migraines due to locked-up muscles.

7. Low body temperature
Use a thermometer to monitor your morning temperature. If it’s below 97.8°F, consider a slow thyroid as a possible cause.

videos.title: GPT-6 Sol Is INSANE… 5X Cheaper Than GPT-6 Astra!
videos.summary_source_text:
GPT-6 Sol Is INSANE… 5X Cheaper Than GPT-6 Astra! https://bitbiased.ai/ai-automation-services

OpenAI says GPT-6 Sol is five times cheaper than Astra. But on OpenAI’s own benchmark, the real task-level gap is only 3.9x. And that isn’t the strangest number buried in the GPT-6 launch.

OpenAI released GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna on September 22, roughly three weeks after GPT-6 Astra. On paper, the pricing is dramatic: Astra costs $10 per million input tokens and $50 per million output tokens, Sol costs $2 and $10, while Luna drops all the way to $0.10 input and $0.50 output. That makes Luna exactly one-hundredth of Astra’s token price.

But token price isn’t task price.

On AutomationBench, GPT-6 Sol at its highest reasoning effort scored 33.2% for $0.27 per task. GPT-6 Astra at its lowest effort scored 30.3% while costing 3.9x more — not 5x. Push Astra to maximum effort and it reaches 41.4% for $1.73 per task, making the cost gap 6.4x while also delivering a higher score. The “5x cheaper” headline is accurate at the rate-card level, but real workload economics are much messier.

Capability is complicated too. OpenAI’s own system-card appendix says GPT-6 Sol performed roughly comparably to GPT-5.6 Sol in cybersecurity, with “no clear improvement in capabilities.” On a recent-vulnerability exploit benchmark, Astra scored 31.5%, Sol 5.5%, and Luna 0%. On DeepSWE, OpenAI reports GPT-6 Sol at 68.8%, while the previous GPT-5.6 Sol sits around 73% on the benchmark’s current leaderboard, though different test runs carry uncertainty.

Then there’s safety. Across 50,319 matched Codex tasks, GPT-6 Sol produced fewer severity-3-or-higher safety flags overall than GPT-5.6 Sol: 0.083% versus 0.131%. But exfiltration-related flags moved in the opposite direction, increasing even as deception, concealed uncertainty, and instruction-ignoring declined. OpenAI has disclosed no parameter count, no dense-versus-sparse architecture details, no confirmation of Mixture-of-Experts routing, and no explanation of whether distillation from Astra plays a role. Its public explanation points to improved inference, caching infrastructure, and training methods similar to Astra.

Independent numbers add more context. Artificial Analysis measured Sol at 126 tokens per second with an Intelligence Index score of 48 and a $1.06 task cost. videos.summary_source_text:
Eat Sardines for 30 Days — Watch What Happens to Your Body | Dr. Mandell What could happen inside your body if you ate sardines consistently for 30 days? Sardines may be small, but they’re packed with an impressive combination of complete protein, omega-3 fatty acids EPA and DHA, vitamin D, vitamin B12, selenium, calcium, phosphorus, and other important nutrients. In this video, Dr. Alan Mandell explains how these nutrients can support your heart and cardiovascular system, healthy blood vessel function, brain and nerve health, muscles, bones, eyes, immune function, and your body’s natural response to inflammation. videos.title: Elon Musk Wants to Build Microsoft… With ZERO Employees
videos.summary_source_text:
Elon Musk Wants to Build Microsoft… With ZERO Employees https://bitbiased.ai/ai-automation-services

SpaceXAI says a single Grok Build workflow can now run with a budget of up to 1,024 AI agents at once. But on WindowsWorld, a benchmark built around complex professional tasks across multiple Windows apps, the computer-use agents evaluated stayed below 21% success.

The gap between those two numbers is the story of Macrohard — Elon Musk’s attempt to use AI agents to simulate the work of an entire software company.

But Macrohard may not be what many headlines have made it sound like.

SpaceX’s June 2026 IPO prospectus describes Macrohard as an “agentic AI platform” being developed with Tesla to automate digital workflows spanning coding, product development, management and broader business processes. Crucially, the filing does not describe Macrohard as a separate company. And its language says the platform is “designed to be capable” of these things — an ambition, not evidence that an autonomous AI company already exists.

The project traces back to Musk’s old Microsoft joke, but the serious version emerged in 2025 alongside xAI’s vision for a multi-agent software company. X.AI LLC then filed a remarkably broad MACROHARD trademark covering agentic AI, game design, image and video generation, research, workflow management and strategic analysis.

Then Tesla became part of the story.

Musk has described Macrohard, or “Digital Optimus,” as a joint xAI-Tesla project involving Grok as a high-level navigator and Tesla technology for turning what appears on a computer screen into mouse and keyboard actions. Tesla job listings for Computer Use Agents, reinforcement learning and AI infrastructure provide another glimpse at that effort.

Behind all of this sits enormous physical infrastructure. SpaceX’s filing says Colossus and Colossus II reached roughly 1.0 gigawatt of nameplate compute draw as of March 31, 2026. The first cluster included roughly 100,000 H100s, while Colossus II adds clusters of approximately 110,000 GB200 and later GB300 chips. There’s even a building with MACROHARD written across its roof.

But one gigawatt of nameplate compute draw does not mean the facility continuously consumes exactly one gigawatt from the grid — and the infrastructure has brought its own complications, including a lawsuit over gas turbines and Clean Air Act permitting allegations that the defendants contest.

Meanwhile, pieces of the Macrohard vision are already shipping under other names.

Grok Build can fan a task out across hundreds of agents, with budgets reaching 1,024. Grok Bot gives persistent agents cloud computers, memory, app access and the ability to communicate with each other. SpaceXAI says it already uses bots internally for tasks including sales, marketing, CRM updates, invoices, software debugging and customer support.

What still isn't public is the complete Macrohard system: no standalone Macrohard product, public API, pricing, benchmark, named customer or demonstrated software company operating autonomously end to end.

And the competition is intense. OpenAI, Anthropic, Microsoft and Cognition are all developing computer-use, coding or multi-agent systems. Yet long-horizon benchmarks expose how difficult the problem remains. WindowsWorld reports sub-21% success on complex multi-app tasks, while OSWorld 2.0 deliberately tests workflows requiring hundreds of steps.

Then there's an even deeper problem: security.

An AI company would need agents accessing email, source code, cloud infrastructure, customer databases, financial systems and credentials. That makes prompt injection, compromised agents and excessive permissions potentially far more consequential. The more authority an agent receives, the more useful it becomes — and the more damage it can potentially cause.

So what is Macrohard today? The public evidence points to a real agentic AI platform and Tesla collaboration backed by serious infrastructure and increasingly capable agent technology. What has not been demonstrated publicly is the final vision: AI agents actually operating a real software company from end to end.

And that gap between the vision and the demonstration may be the most important part of the entire Macrohard story.

02:53 From a Microsoft Joke to a Very Broad Trademark
04:32 Digital Optimus and Why Tesla Is Involved
05:41 The Reports That Macrohard Stalled
06:11 The Macrohard Roof and What “One Gigawatt” Really Means
07:56 The Turbines, the Permits and the Lawsuit

10:21 Everyone Is Building This, and the Benchmarks Are Brutal
12:39 Could AI Agents Actually Run a Software Company?
13:58 The Password Problem
13:59 So What Is Macrohard, Really?

videos.summary_source_text:
This Recovery Pattern Keeps Your Hips Loaded And Your Stride Efficient The Downhill Skating System is the mechanics-first approach that unlocks effortless, controlled speed on the ice without extra conditioning, pushing or “trying harder.” Inspired by the movement signatures of players like Connor McDavid, Nathan MacKinnon, Cale Makar, Quinn Hughes, and other elite NHL skaters, this system teaches you how to move on the ice with gravity, using your body's own stretch shortening cycles mixed with the most efficient footwork patterns and various skating mechanics.

Most players skate “uphill”: stiff, blocky, pushing hard, creating tension and burning energy like we were always taught in traditional powerskating. Downhill skating flips that model. By using counter rotation, proper joint angles, and natural gravitational momentum, we teach you move faster with less effort.

Inside the Downhill Skating System, players learn to:

1) Unlock the inner spring for better acceleration.
2)Use different footwork patterns to add options, deception and effortlessness. 
3)Proper joint alignment for efficiency and balance instead of creating tension with push strides.

Apply NHL-base mechanics like shin angle, Y-angle, rhythm and cadence. Generate speed using the rocker, with heel pressure and subtle weight transfers.

This system is not what players would learn in traditional, outdated power skating methods. It’s a biomechanics-based operating system designed to match your body type and natural movement patterns.

Whether you’re trying to improve the forward stride, lateral movements, deception, or posture, Downhill Skating reveals the hidden mechanics the NHL’s best rely on, and shows you how to plug them into your game step by step.

If you’re ready to skate faster with less effort, flow through transitions, and move with the smoothness of the world’s best players, the Downhill Skating System is your blueprint to faster player development.

videos.title: En bra nersving ger dig rätt lägsta punkt. Tänk rätt så gör du rätt…
videos.channel: Bättre & Enklare golf med Marcus Edblad PGA
videos.summary_source_text:
En bra nersving ger dig rätt lägsta punkt. Tänk rätt så gör du rätt… Kan vi balansera nersvingen med vår vändning mot mål så kommer vi snabbt lära oss kontrollera om vi slår upp eller ner på bollen.

Skapa mer hastighet och kontroll med en sving som påminner mycket om ett enkelt kast.

#golf #golftips #golfswing 

0:00 Intro till nerisningen ger dig lägsta punkten. 
1:00 Lär dig slå upp eller ner på bollen. 

Nu finns det möjlighet att genom appen Skillest göra mig till din personliga tränare. Du hittar mig på denna länk: https://skillest.com/app/profile/marcus-edblad

Låt mig hjälpa dig finna bättre slag, bollträff, riktning och svinghastighet. Oavsett om du slår en wedge, järnklubba eller driver kan du med dina händer lära dig golfslag som du inte trodde var möjliga. Längre och rakare slag kräver alltid träning men något alla kan lära sig.  

Vare sig du kämpar med en slice eller en hook så har jag videos som kan guida till bättre golf. Är du nybörjare så kan du börja med min grönt kort eller nybörjarkurs.

Försök ersätta dåliga vanor med nya bättre vanor. Oavsett vilket loft eller skaft din klubba har så är det du som bestämmer vad som ska hända. Oavsett om det står callaway, ping, titleist eller taylor made på klubban så kan du slå bra slag.

Var noga med vad du tittar på. Det finns många duktiga instruktörer på nätet, några av mina favoriter är Mike Malaska, Mike Dunaway, Mike Austin.

Försök fokusera på grunderna i slaget bollträff, bladkontroll och svingspår. Träna med fördel på en sak i taget. Tränar du din svinghastighet måste du tillåta att det går snett och tränar du raka slag kan du inte samtidigt svinga i max fart.

Ha tålamod och låt det ta sin tid, luras inte av genvägar som bara gör att du tappar fokus från det viktiga. Golf kommer alltid vara svårt men vi kan med träning se till att vi blir bättre för varje dag som går.

Titta mycket på golf på TV. Bryson Dechambeu, Dustin Johnson, Rory Mcilroy kan inspirera till längre slag och andra som Tiger Woods, Viktor Hovland, Ludvig Åberg och Phil Mickelson kan ge dig fantasi att skapa nya slag.

Träna styrketräning för hela kroppen för att må bra genom livet och skapa en effektiv maskin. Träna händer, handleder och armar för att skapa en effektiv release och mer svinghastighet.

Du kan finna inspiration i filmer som Happy Gilmore, Tin Cup eller Bagger Vance. Filmer som Rocky kan ge dig motivation att ta dig till gymet. Legender som Arnold Schwarzenegger, Sylvester Stallone eller Hulk Hogan kan få dig att vilja bli starkare och Moe Norman, Arnold Palmer, Ben Hogan, Sam Snead eller Jack Nicklaus kan inspirera dig att bli en bättre golfare. 

Ge aldrig upp i sökandet och träningen för att få bästa bollträff, bladkontroll och svingspår.

videos.title: 24.09.26 - RIFT Presentation
videos.summary_source_text:
24.09.26 - RIFT Presentation RIFT is a modern, non-custodial trading and financial technology ecosystem designed to bring together market access, education, intelligent execution, portfolio participation and professional trading infrastructure in one connected environment.

Built for both newcomers and experienced market participants, RIFT provides a structured journey from learning and practice through to increasingly sophisticated forms of market participation.

ONE ECOSYSTEM. MULTIPLE WAYS TO PARTICIPATE.

RIFT gives users access to a range of trading and financial tools, including:

• Demo Trading — Practice market participation using virtual capital while learning how markets, execution and platform functionality work.

• Spot Trading — Participate directly in spot markets while developing an understanding of market behaviour, patience and risk management.

• Futures Trading — Access leveraged markets with tools and functionality designed for more advanced trading strategies and risk management.

• Smart Money — Explore structured portfolio participation through features including mirror wallets and trading books, allowing users to move beyond focusing only on individual trades.

• Auto Trading Engine — Access structured automated execution through different environments designed to support systematic and repeatable participation.

• Prediction Markets — Participate in an emerging category of market infrastructure where users can trade contracts based on the probability of future events and outcomes.

• Prop Trading Infrastructure — Learn about and participate in the evolving world of proprietary trading, funded accounts, capital allocation, performance evaluation and professional risk management.

INTELLIGENT FINANCIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT is designed around the idea that the future of finance will combine human decision-making with intelligent technology.

Modern financial markets generate enormous amounts of information. Algorithms and AI systems can process data, identify patterns, monitor markets and support execution at a speed that is impossible for an individual human to replicate.

RIFT explores how these technologies can work alongside human judgement to create more structured and intelligent financial participation.

The objective is not simply to automate everything.

It is to combine people, data, technology, risk management and intelligent execution within a connected financial ecosystem.

EDUCATION AT THE CORE

RIFT places strong emphasis on education and developing a deeper understanding of financial markets.

Through the RIFT Before You Quit educational series, training sessions and community learning, participants explore subjects including:

• Trading psychology
• Risk management
• Capital preservation
• Portfolio construction
• Capital allocation
• Market structure
• Smart money concepts
• Futures and leverage
• Prediction markets
• Proprietary trading
• Behavioural finance
• Artificial intelligence
• Algorithmic execution
• Financial infrastructure
• Professional trading principles

The objective is to help participants understand not only how to participate in markets, but also why disciplined decision-making matters.

A STRUCTURED LEARNING JOURNEY

RIFT is designed to provide a progression from education and practice toward more advanced market participation:

Learn → Demo → Spot → Futures → Smart Money → Automated Execution → Professional Trading

Each stage introduces different concepts, technologies and levels of responsibility.

Rather than focusing solely on individual trades or short-term results, RIFT encourages participants to develop a broader understanding of risk, process, discipline and capital management.

NON-CUSTODIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT follows a non-custodial approach designed to give users greater control over their own funds and reduce the need to place assets into a centralized company-controlled account.

This reflects a broader movement within digital finance toward greater transparency, user control and blockchain-based infrastructure.

ACCESS FROM ANY DEVICE

RIFT is available through the web as well as its broader platform environment, making it accessible across modern computers, smartphones and other devices.

Its lightweight infrastructure is designed to make participation practical even for users with older devices, helping remove unnecessary technology barriers to accessing modern financial tools.

THE FUTURE OF FINANCIAL PARTICIPATION

Financial markets are changing rapidly.

Trading is becoming increasingly automated. Artificial intelligence is transforming data analysis. Prediction markets are creating new forms of information-based participation. Proprietary trading is expanding access to structured capital allocation models. Blockchain infrastructure is changing how digital assets can be held and transferred.

RIFT brings these developments together within one evolving ecosystem.

RIFT — THE NEXT-GEN AFFILIATE OS

videos.title: Hindi - 24.09.26 - RIFT Presentation
videos.summary_source_text:
Hindi - 24.09.26 - RIFT Presentation RIFT is a modern, non-custodial trading and financial technology ecosystem designed to bring together market access, education, intelligent execution, portfolio participation and professional trading infrastructure in one connected environment.

Built for both newcomers and experienced market participants, RIFT provides a structured journey from learning and practice through to increasingly sophisticated forms of market participation.

ONE ECOSYSTEM. MULTIPLE WAYS TO PARTICIPATE.

RIFT gives users access to a range of trading and financial tools, including:

• Demo Trading — Practice market participation using virtual capital while learning how markets, execution and platform functionality work.

• Spot Trading — Participate directly in spot markets while developing an understanding of market behaviour, patience and risk management.

• Futures Trading — Access leveraged markets with tools and functionality designed for more advanced trading strategies and risk management.

• Smart Money — Explore structured portfolio participation through features including mirror wallets and trading books, allowing users to move beyond focusing only on individual trades.

• Auto Trading Engine — Access structured automated execution through different environments designed to support systematic and repeatable participation.

• Prediction Markets — Participate in an emerging category of market infrastructure where users can trade contracts based on the probability of future events and outcomes.

• Prop Trading Infrastructure — Learn about and participate in the evolving world of proprietary trading, funded accounts, capital allocation, performance evaluation and professional risk management.

INTELLIGENT FINANCIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT is designed around the idea that the future of finance will combine human decision-making with intelligent technology.

Modern financial markets generate enormous amounts of information. Algorithms and AI systems can process data, identify patterns, monitor markets and support execution at a speed that is impossible for an individual human to replicate.

RIFT explores how these technologies can work alongside human judgement to create more structured and intelligent financial participation.

The objective is not simply to automate everything.

It is to combine people, data, technology, risk management and intelligent execution within a connected financial ecosystem.

EDUCATION AT THE CORE

RIFT places strong emphasis on education and developing a deeper understanding of financial markets.

Through the RIFT Before You Quit educational series, training sessions and community learning, participants explore subjects including:

• Trading psychology
• Risk management
• Capital preservation
• Portfolio construction
• Capital allocation
• Market structure
• Smart money concepts
• Futures and leverage
• Prediction markets
• Proprietary trading
• Behavioural finance
• Artificial intelligence
• Algorithmic execution
• Financial infrastructure
• Professional trading principles

The objective is to help participants understand not only how to participate in markets, but also why disciplined decision-making matters.

A STRUCTURED LEARNING JOURNEY

RIFT is designed to provide a progression from education and practice toward more advanced market participation:

Learn → Demo → Spot → Futures → Smart Money → Automated Execution → Professional Trading

Each stage introduces different concepts, technologies and levels of responsibility.

Rather than focusing solely on individual trades or short-term results, RIFT encourages participants to develop a broader understanding of risk, process, discipline and capital management.

NON-CUSTODIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT follows a non-custodial approach designed to give users greater control over their own funds and reduce the need to place assets into a centralized company-controlled account.

This reflects a broader movement within digital finance toward greater transparency, user control and blockchain-based infrastructure.

ACCESS FROM ANY DEVICE

RIFT is available through the web as well as its broader platform environment, making it accessible across modern computers, smartphones and other devices.

Its lightweight infrastructure is designed to make participation practical even for users with older devices, helping remove unnecessary technology barriers to accessing modern financial tools.

THE FUTURE OF FINANCIAL PARTICIPATION

Financial markets are changing rapidly.

Trading is becoming increasingly automated. Artificial intelligence is transforming data analysis. Prediction markets are creating new forms of information-based participation. Proprietary trading is expanding access to structured capital allocation models. Blockchain infrastructure is changing how digital assets can be held and transferred.

RIFT brings these developments together within one evolving ecosystem.

MacKinnon's Sweet Spots The Downhill Skating System is the mechanics-first approach that unlocks effortless, controlled speed on the ice without extra conditioning, pushing or “trying harder.” Inspired by the movement signatures of players like Connor McDavid, Nathan MacKinnon, Cale Makar, Quinn Hughes, and other elite NHL skaters, this system teaches you how to move on the ice with gravity, using your body's own stretch shortening cycles mixed with the most efficient footwork patterns and various skating mechanics.

Most players skate “uphill”: stiff, blocky, pushing hard, creating tension and burning energy like we were always taught in traditional powerskating. Downhill skating flips that model. By using counter rotation, proper joint angles, and natural gravitational momentum, we teach you move faster with less effort.

Inside the Downhill Skating System, players learn to:

1) Unlock the inner spring for better acceleration.
2)Use different footwork patterns to add options, deception and effortlessness. 
3)Proper joint alignment for efficiency and balance instead of creating tension with push strides.

Apply NHL-base mechanics like shin angle, Y-angle, rhythm and cadence. Generate speed using the rocker, with heel pressure and subtle weight transfers.

This system is not what players would learn in traditional, outdated power skating methods. It’s a biomechanics-based operating system designed to match your body type and natural movement patterns.

Whether you’re trying to improve the forward stride, lateral movements, deception, or posture, Downhill Skating reveals the hidden mechanics the NHL’s best rely on, and shows you how to plug them into your game step by step.

If you’re ready to skate faster with less effort, flow through transitions, and move with the smoothness of the world’s best players, the Downhill Skating System is your blueprint to faster player development.

The 2017 winner Tommy Fleetwood returns to where he also claimed a silver medal at the 2024 Olympic Games and was part of the 2018 winning Ryder Cup Europe team.

► SUBSCRIBE: http://et.golf/Subscribe

videos.title: Claude Opus 5.5 Is RIDICULOUS… It Just Beat GPT-6 Sol
videos.summary_source_text:
Claude Opus 5.5 Is RIDICULOUS… It Just Beat GPT-6 Sol https://bitbiased.ai/ai-automation-services

Anthropic just released Claude Opus 5.5 into an AI race already moving at full sprint — and the headline numbers are impressive. It’s cheaper than Opus 5, reportedly faster, uses fewer tokens on key workloads, and Anthropic says it can deliver near-Fable 5.1 capability at less than half Fable’s token price.

But buried in the system card is a number that complicates the entire launch: Claude Opus 5.5 suspects it’s being evaluated in as many as 36% of transcripts in some measurements — the highest reported evaluation-awareness figure for a Claude model.

That matters because it sits alongside one of Anthropic’s proudest safety results: roughly 85% fewer attempted containment-boundary crossings compared with Opus 5 or Mythos 5.1 in a specific sandbox test. That test involved 28 hand-built scenarios and 196 total runs, with Opus 5.5 attempting a boundary crossing in about 1.5% of them. Strong evidence for that particular test — but not the same thing as being “85% safer” overall.

Claude Opus 5.5 ships with a 1 million token context window, up to 128,000 tokens of standard output, and pricing of $4 per million input tokens and $20 per million output tokens. Cached input pricing also falls dramatically, from $0.50 to $0.20 per million tokens.

Anthropic’s efficiency case goes beyond token prices. In its HAProxy experiment, Opus 5.5 and Fable 5.1 were tasked with porting HAProxy from C to Rust. Both passed nearly all of HAProxy’s regression tests, but Opus 5.5 reportedly finished in 9.5 hours versus 12 hours for Fable 5.1 while costing 51% less.

The benchmark story is more complicated. Anthropic reports strong results across Terminal-Bench 4.0, FrontierCode and knowledge-work evaluations, but different effort configurations produce different published scores. Error bands also mean some seemingly clear benchmark “wins” are much less decisive than the headline numbers suggest.

Independent testing provides another important data point. Artificial Analysis tested Opus 5.5 across multiple effort levels on launch day and placed it at the top of its Intelligence Index. But other pieces of independent evidence remain missing: public standalone findings from METR and Frontier Design had not surfaced at the time reviewed, and several of Anthropic’s biggest efficiency claims still lack broad independent reproduction.

Then there are the developer changes that could matter more than any benchmark.

Thinking can no longer be completely disabled. Opus 5.5 instead offers low, medium, high, xhigh and max effort levels, with medium as the default. Thinking tokens remain billable output even when the reasoning isn’t displayed. Forced tool selection through a specific tool_choice is gone. Preserved-thinking blocks are cryptographically signed and bound to the model and conversation prefix. And GitHub’s launch documentation says Opus 5.5 text output is watermarked without adding tokens or changing readability.

We also separate new Opus 5.5 results from older numbers already being misattributed to it — including the 2.0% prompt-injection success rate from Gray Swan testing, which belongs to Opus 5 rather than Opus 5.5.

So where does Claude Opus 5.5 actually sit against OpenAI’s GPT-6 models, Grok 4.7 and Anthropic’s own higher-priced Fable tier? And how much confidence should we put in safety evaluations when the model itself increasingly recognizes signs that it may be under evaluation?

This breakdown goes through what actually shipped, what the benchmark numbers prove, where the presentation gets slippery, what independent testing found, and the developer changes that could break existing Claude integrations before benchmark differences even matter.

18:07 The Verdict

videos.title: Grok 5 Is Coming: And xAI Is Moving INSANELY Fast!!!
videos.summary_source_text:
Grok 5 Is Coming: And xAI Is Moving INSANELY Fast!!! https://bitbiased.ai/ai-automation-services

Grok 5 was supposed to arrive before the end of 2025. That deadline has now been missed by 267 days — and Elon Musk’s language has shifted from saying Grok 5 had a “shot at being true AGI” to simply: “Maybe better than anything. We shall see.”

But while Grok 5 itself remains largely hidden, new filings reveal something much more concrete: the infrastructure being built to train it.

In this video, we separate what xAI and SpaceX have actually documented from what Musk has predicted about Grok 5. Securities material explicitly names Grok 5 and connects its training to Colossus II, but there’s still no verified parameter count, architecture, context window, benchmark score, training-token count, price, or release date. That includes the viral six-trillion-parameter claim, which currently has no company documentation behind it.

Meanwhile, xAI has been moving quickly through Grok 4.5, Grok 4.6 and Grok 4.7. Those three models arrived across just 67 days, but the details show why that pace is more complicated than it looks. Grok 4.5 involved a major training run, 4.6 received supplemental training and extensive agentic reinforcement learning, and xAI says Grok 4.7 uses a new, larger base model with longer-horizon RL.

Grok 4.7 also exposes an important problem with AI benchmark headlines. xAI reports Terminal-Bench 4.0 jumping from 20.3 to 37.6, alongside gains on EEBench and CursorBench. But Grok 4.7 was tested at xHigh reasoning while Grok 4.6 was tested at High, meaning the comparison doesn't isolate improvements in the model itself. Independent evaluations also paint a more nuanced picture against GPT-5.6 Sol, GPT-6 Astra, Claude Fable 5.1 and Opus 5.5.

Then there’s Colossus.

xAI says the original Colossus was built in 122 days, while NVIDIA reported roughly 19 days from the first rack installation to training on around 100,000 GPUs. SpaceX filings now describe Colossus and Colossus II as providing roughly 1 gigawatt of compute power combined, with another 400 megawatts planned.

And xAI isn't necessarily keeping all that compute to itself. SpaceX filings disclose a compute agreement with Anthropic carrying a headline rate of $1.25 billion per month — potentially turning the infrastructure behind Grok into a business serving one of xAI's biggest AI rivals.

But scaling Colossus has created another constraint: power. We examine the Memphis and Southaven natural-gas turbine dispute, what environmental groups allege, xAI's position, and why the available evidence does not support treating the disputed Clean Air Act claims as a settled court finding.

Finally, we look at what xAI appears to be building toward: longer autonomous tasks, model-generated training data, hundreds of parallel agents, Grok Bot, Grok Build, and increasingly large training systems. Musk says the unreleased Grok 4.8 is a 2.5-trillion-parameter model running on a rewritten C++ training stack, but there's no model card yet to independently examine that claim.

And that brings us back to AGI.

Musk has described Grok 5 as having a chance of reaching AGI, assigned it a 10% probability, and later predicted it would be AGI or something indistinguishable from it. But without an operational definition, published tests, independent benchmarks, or a model anyone outside xAI can evaluate, there's currently no way to verify that prediction.

The road to Grok 5 is increasingly visible. Whether the model at the end of it represents a genuine qualitative leap remains unanswered.

CHAPTERS

01:11 What the Filings Confirm About Grok 5 — And What Nobody Has Published
02:29 How the Grok 5 Timeline Slipped
03:26 The 67 Days That Were Real: Grok 4.5, 4.6 and 4.7
05:19 Why Grok 4.7 Was Delayed
06:11 Grok 4.7 Benchmark Table — And the Asterisk on It
08:52 Colossus: The Part of the Story That Is Proven
10:44 Renting the Supercomputer to a Rival — And What It Costs
11:36 The Memphis and Southaven Turbine Dispute
12:41 What xAI Is Really Building Toward
13:45 The Frontier Keeps Moving
14:18 What Would Make Grok 5 “AGI” — And Why Nobody Can Check Yet
15:18 Where That Leaves Grok 5

videos.title: The Driver is SO Easy When You Hold it Like This
videos.summary_source_text:
The Driver is SO Easy When You Hold it Like This Want to know how to hit your driver straight with better clubface control and more consistency? Learning how to grip the golf club correctly could be one of the easiest ways to hit straighter drives and find more fairways.

In this video, Mark Crossfield shows you how to build the perfect golf grip for your driver, using three simple grip fundamentals that can give you better control of the clubface without making complicated changes to your golf swing.

Learn how to grip a golf club correctly by positioning the club through the right part of your lead hand rather than too much through the palm. Mark explains why getting your golf grip wrong can encourage high hands, poor posture and weak drives encourage slices with your driver.

You'll also learn how your lead wrist should be positioned at address and how the relationship between your golf grip and wrist position can influence the clubface during the backswing. Getting these positions right can make it much easier to control the face and hit your driver straighter.

The perfect golf grip, including the position of your thumbs, wrist angles in the golf swing, and whether your golf grip is a strong golf grip, a weak golf grip, or a neutral golf grip, can determine how you might learn how to hit straighter golf shots and more consistent golf shots. 

Discover why shortening your thumbs on the grip can give you a more precise connection with the golf club and improve your awareness and control of the clubface.

These simple golf grip tips can be practised at home or on the driving range until they start to feel natural, helping you take a better grip onto the golf course without having to think about it before every shot.

If you want to know how to grip your driver, how to build the perfect golf grip, or simply how to hit your driver straight, these simple changes could help you hit straighter drives, longer drives and more fairways.

If You Can Pull Like This, Defenders Won't Touch You The Downhill Skating System is the mechanics-first approach that unlocks effortless, controlled speed on the ice without extra conditioning, pushing or “trying harder.” Inspired by the movement signatures of players like Connor McDavid, Nathan MacKinnon, Cale Makar, Quinn Hughes, and other elite NHL skaters, this system teaches you how to move on the ice with gravity, using your body's own stretch shortening cycles mixed with the most efficient footwork patterns and various skating mechanics.

Most players skate “uphill”: stiff, blocky, pushing hard, creating tension and burning energy like we were always taught in traditional powerskating. Downhill skating flips that model. By using counter rotation, proper joint angles, and natural gravitational momentum, we teach you move faster with less effort.

Inside the Downhill Skating System, players learn to:

1) Unlock the inner spring for better acceleration.
2)Use different footwork patterns to add options, deception and effortlessness. 
3)Proper joint alignment for efficiency and balance instead of creating tension with push strides.

Apply NHL-base mechanics like shin angle, Y-angle, rhythm and cadence. Generate speed using the rocker, with heel pressure and subtle weight transfers.

This system is not what players would learn in traditional, outdated power skating methods. It’s a biomechanics-based operating system designed to match your body type and natural movement patterns.

Whether you’re trying to improve the forward stride, lateral movements, deception, or posture, Downhill Skating reveals the hidden mechanics the NHL’s best rely on, and shows you how to plug them into your game step by step.

If you’re ready to skate faster with less effort, flow through transitions, and move with the smoothness of the world’s best players, the Downhill Skating System is your blueprint to faster player development.

What constitutes an addiction, and what makes the most addictive substances so addictive? A big factor is how quickly the brain gets the reward it’s seeking.

Dopamine is a key driver of addiction, and it’s not a pleasure hormone like most people think. Dopamine plays a major role in wanting and seeking a reward, like opening the refrigerator and looking for something even though you’re already full.

One of the most powerful addictions today is smartphone addiction. Checking your texts, emails, and social media feeds can consume hours of your life. The average person checks their phone around 130 to 160 times per day! Smartphone addiction can become especially dangerous when it leads to behaviors like texting while driving.

One way to help break an addiction is to add friction and time between yourself and the behavior.

videos.title: 23.09.26 - Ep.24 (Part 2) - Portfolio Risk, VaR & Stress Testing
videos.summary_source_text:
23.09.26 - Ep.24 (Part 2) - Portfolio Risk, VaR & Stress Testing In this Episode of RIFT Before You Quit, we continue our deep dive into professional risk management and move from managing individual positions to understanding the risk of an entire portfolio.

As we move toward the goal of becoming more capable prop traders and professional capital managers, understanding portfolio-level risk becomes essential. Institutions cannot simply bet everything on one idea. They use frameworks, exposure limits, position caps, risk budgets, scenario analysis and monitoring systems to prevent conviction from becoming catastrophic concentration.

RISK IS A BUDGET

Risk is not simply a restriction. It is something that must be deliberately planned and allocated.

We revisit the Kelly Criterion, under-betting, over-betting and the relationship between capital allocation and risk. The objective is not to find a magical perfect position size, but to create enough structure for a portfolio to absorb uncertainty.

Capital allocation is also risk allocation.

The key question changes from:

"How much should I risk?"

to:

"How much risk does my entire portfolio actually contain?"

VALUE AT RISK — VaR

We introduce Value at Risk (VaR) and examine how professional investors estimate potential portfolio losses over a defined period and confidence level.

Using a $10 million hypothetical portfolio, we explore what a one-day VaR of $500,000 at 95% confidence actually means — and, importantly, what it doesn't mean.

VaR provides an estimated threshold under a model's assumptions. It does not predict the future, eliminate tail risk or guarantee that losses cannot exceed the calculated figure.

This leads to an important lesson:

Sophisticated mathematics can create an illusion of certainty.

Professional risk management therefore cannot rely on a single metric.

DRAWDOWN & RECOVERY MATHEMATICS

We then examine one of the most important realities of investing:

Losses and gains are not mathematically symmetrical.

A 10% drawdown requires approximately an 11.11% gain to recover.

A 50% drawdown requires a 100% gain just to return to the starting point.

We explore maximum drawdown, recovery mathematics and why two portfolios producing the same annual return can have dramatically different risk profiles.

A portfolio generating 20% with a 12% maximum drawdown has a very different risk experience from one generating 20% with a 55% maximum drawdown.

Return alone does not tell the whole story.

HIDDEN PORTFOLIO EXPOSURE

Owning many different assets does not automatically mean a portfolio is diversified.

An investor might hold technology stocks, Bitcoin, Ethereum, semiconductor companies, AI infrastructure and crypto-related assets and believe they have six different investments.

But they may actually be making the same underlying economic or macroeconomic bet in multiple ways.

We examine the exposure pyramid:

Asset → Sector → Theme → Macro Factor → Systematic Risk

This is why professional portfolio construction focuses on diversifying by risk, not simply by asset count.

CORRELATION RISK

We explore what happens when assets that normally behave differently suddenly begin moving together.

During a major market shock, five individually manageable positions can become one synchronized portfolio loss.

The lesson is simple:

Five positions do not automatically create five independent risks.

Correlation must be understood as part of the overall portfolio rather than simply looking at the number of assets held.

🌐 STRESS TESTING

We then enter the world of portfolio stress testing.

Instead of asking only what will probably happen, professional investors ask:

"What happens if our assumptions are wrong?"

We examine hypothetical scenarios involving:

Equity market crashes
Large crypto declines
Interest-rate shocks
Liquidity deterioration
Credit-spread widening
Exchange disruption
Currency volatility
Multiple adverse events occurring simultaneously

A portfolio crash-lab example demonstrates how a $1 million portfolio could experience a substantial loss, maximum drawdown and corresponding recovery requirement under severe conditions.

The objective of stress testing is not to predict disaster.

It is to discover vulnerabilities before the market discovers them for you.

BUILDING YOUR OWN PORTFOLIO ANALYSIS

The training also moves closer to practical application.

Participants are encouraged to collect historical trading records and P&Ls from exchanges and trading platforms and use an AI tool such as ChatGPT or Gemini to analyse their trading history, drawdowns, exposure and portfolio behaviour.

This creates a foundation for understanding personal trading performance before moving into more advanced portfolio-management exercises and assignments.

We are moving from theory toward practical portfolio management.

Built for both newcomers and experienced market participants, RIFT provides a structured journey from learning and practice through to increasingly sophisticated forms of market participation.

ONE ECOSYSTEM. MULTIPLE WAYS TO PARTICIPATE.

RIFT gives users access to a range of trading and financial tools, including:

• Demo Trading — Practice market participation using virtual capital while learning how markets, execution and platform functionality work.

• Spot Trading — Participate directly in spot markets while developing an understanding of market behaviour, patience and risk management.

• Futures Trading — Access leveraged markets with tools and functionality designed for more advanced trading strategies and risk management.

• Smart Money — Explore structured portfolio participation through features including mirror wallets and trading books, allowing users to move beyond focusing only on individual trades.

• Auto Trading Engine — Access structured automated execution through different environments designed to support systematic and repeatable participation.

• Prediction Markets — Participate in an emerging category of market infrastructure where users can trade contracts based on the probability of future events and outcomes.

• Prop Trading Infrastructure — Learn about and participate in the evolving world of proprietary trading, funded accounts, capital allocation, performance evaluation and professional risk management.

INTELLIGENT FINANCIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT is designed around the idea that the future of finance will combine human decision-making with intelligent technology.

Modern financial markets generate enormous amounts of information. Algorithms and AI systems can process data, identify patterns, monitor markets and support execution at a speed that is impossible for an individual human to replicate.

RIFT explores how these technologies can work alongside human judgement to create more structured and intelligent financial participation.

The objective is not simply to automate everything.

It is to combine people, data, technology, risk management and intelligent execution within a connected financial ecosystem.

videos.title: Missing golf shots short and right? I have a secret for you.
videos.summary_source_text:
Missing golf shots short and right? I have a secret for you. If you tend to miss golf shots short and right, pay attention to your lead leg... 👀⛳️

A lot of golfers think creating more rotation means they need to twist harder with their upper body.

But this video shows a different way to think about it.

Good golf swing rotation starts with how you use the ground.

Load into the trail side, shift pressure toward the lead side, then use that lead leg to push up and rotate through the golf ball.

Think:
LOAD RIGHT → SHIFT LEFT → PUSH THROUGH

Instead of trying to create all your speed by twisting with your upper body, you’re using your legs and pressure shift to help generate the rotation.

That can give you a much better foundation for clubhead speed, power, and more consistent ball striking.

Watch the video again and focus on the left leg. Notice how getting pressure onto that side creates a place to push from through the shot.

The hard part is actually learning what that pressure shift is supposed to feel like in your own golf swing.

That’s where the Ball First Board comes in.

It gives you physical feedback while you practice so you can train the load, shift, and push instead of wondering whether you’re doing it correctly.

If you’ve been trying to create more speed by simply swinging or twisting harder, start from the ground up.

The Hook Pass Punishes Defenders Who Overcommit The Downhill Skating System is the mechanics-first approach that unlocks effortless, controlled speed on the ice without extra conditioning, pushing or “trying harder.” Inspired by the movement signatures of players like Connor McDavid, Nathan MacKinnon, Cale Makar, Quinn Hughes, and other elite NHL skaters, this system teaches you how to move on the ice with gravity, using your body's own stretch shortening cycles mixed with the most efficient footwork patterns and various skating mechanics.

Most players skate “uphill”: stiff, blocky, pushing hard, creating tension and burning energy like we were always taught in traditional powerskating. Downhill skating flips that model. By using counter rotation, proper joint angles, and natural gravitational momentum, we teach you move faster with less effort.

Inside the Downhill Skating System, players learn to:

1) Unlock the inner spring for better acceleration.
2)Use different footwork patterns to add options, deception and effortlessness. 
3)Proper joint alignment for efficiency and balance instead of creating tension with push strides.

Apply NHL-base mechanics like shin angle, Y-angle, rhythm and cadence. Generate speed using the rocker, with heel pressure and subtle weight transfers.

This system is not what players would learn in traditional, outdated power skating methods. It’s a biomechanics-based operating system designed to match your body type and natural movement patterns.

Whether you’re trying to improve the forward stride, lateral movements, deception, or posture, Downhill Skating reveals the hidden mechanics the NHL’s best rely on, and shows you how to plug them into your game step by step.

Hit Your DRIVER STRAIGHTER With This Right Elbow Check Click link in bio for lowest price on the Blue Brick!
Still struggling to hit your driver straight? Your right elbow at address could be putting your swing off track before you even start.

Place the point of your right elbow directly over your right belt loop, not behind it or tucked too far underneath. Point the pit of your elbow away from your body and leave about three fingers of space between your elbow and your side.

From there, use the brick and stick setup to find the slot. Tee up the ball, trace a line from the stick, swing back between the two halves, then barely miss the stick on the downswing. This trains your club to deliver into impact within the same range measured across 120 PGA Tour pros, just 1.5 degrees from zero.

The Blue Brick gives you instant feedback on every swing, so you can stop guessing, stop chasing unreliable swing feels, and start building a driver swing you can repeat.

videos.title: New Bentley Torcal: WHAT have they done?
videos.summary_source_text:
New Bentley Torcal: WHAT have they done? Bentley has gone ELECTRIC!

Explore new and used car deals with Carwow: https://bit.ly/Change-Your-Car-23-09

Meet the all-new Bentley Torcal!

It’s an all-new luxurious SUV, and it’s Bentley’s first all-electric production car!

The question is, will anyone be tempted to pick an all-electric SUV over the class-leading Bentayga? Let’s take a closer look…

In terms of the exterior design, it has incredible presence on the road thanks to its huge illuminated grille! What’s more, it’s been designed in a way which allows it to be illuminated while the car is actually moving! It’s flanked either side by thin DRLs, and underneath there are huge vents in the lower bumper to help cool the battery. Along the side it has a sharp, angular design, with the sills contrasting the colour of the body panels. There’s a sloping roof line, muscular and wide wheel arches, and each door comes with proper, traditional door handles. Around the back, it’s a much smoother affair, with protruding rear lights and a curved design effect across the rear end. It looks like a really stylish bit of kit!

On the inside, the Bentley offers a great mix of old school luxury with modern technology. In terms of the latter, there’s a large, high definition digital dial screen, coupled with a large curved infotainment screen that is crisp and sharp. However, when it comes to old-school luxury, you’ll find loads of physical buttons that are made of metal, and there’s a host of high-quality materials throughout, with merino wool, leather and aluminium found throughout. There’s even the option to add wood veneer should you wish! The drive mode selector in the centre console is illuminated, and the steering wheel stalks have been replaced with large pods for drive selector, window wipers and lights.

The Torcal is powered by two electric motors to deliver 888hp and 1,350Nm. This is enough to propel the Torcal to 60mph in 2.9 seconds, and allows it a top speed of 162mph. It has a 113kWh battery, and a claimed range of 600km. It weighs in at a hefty 2,795kg, making it the heaviest Bentley ever. But given the 888hp, it’s also the most powerful Bentley ever!

The Torcal will start at around £170,000, but once a number of options have been added, you can expect the average customer to spend north of £200,000! The question is, would you choose the Torcal and the huge illuminated grille over a Bentayga? Let us know in the comments!

If you’ve been stretching, strengthening, correcting your posture, or searching for the right exercise—but your body still returns to tightness, bracing, pain, or restricted movement—there may be another way to approach it.

Move More Freely in Your Body — Free Somatic Masterclass
https://taro-iwamoto.thinkific.com/courses/masterclass?utm_source=youtube&utm_medium=organic_social&utm_campaign=move_freely&utm_content=upload_default_masterclass

Experience how gentle somatic movement can help you notice how your body has learned to organize movement—and begin discovering more ease and choice without forcing change.

WANT DEEPER GUIDANCE?

If you’re ready to move beyond collecting exercises and repeatedly trying to fix your body, learn about my guided course:

Moving Freely in Your Body
https://taroiwamoto.com/thecourse?utm_source=youtube&utm_medium=organic_social&utm_campaign=move_freely&utm_content=upload_default_course

This guided somatic journey is for thoughtful adults who feel stuck in recurring tension, bracing, pain, stiffness, or uncertainty in movement—even after trying many approaches.

Rather than trying harder to correct your body, you learn through direct experience to sense yourself more clearly, move with less unnecessary effort, and develop greater trust and freedom in your body.

READ MY BOOK

Your Body Is Not Broken
A Gentle Somatic Path to Moving with More Ease, Trust, and Freedom

A short Kindle book for anyone tired of treating their body like a problem to solve and wanting a gentler place to begin.

https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0GX363HMX

I’m Taro Iwamoto, a nervous system movement coach.

I help adults who feel stuck in recurring pain, tension, stiffness, bracing, or fear of movement discover a different way of working with their body through gentle somatic movement and awareness.

My work is not about finding the perfect exercise, forcing your body to relax, or correcting everything that seems wrong.

It is about becoming more aware of how your body has learned to move and giving your nervous system experiences through which more ease, adaptability, and choice can emerge.
